   ```bash
   fi
   ```

4. **Insert `BASH_VERSINFO` guards** at the top of each nameref-heavy script. Insertion point is immediately after `set -euo pipefail` (or equivalent). Template:

   ```bash
   # Bash 4.3+ required — this script uses `local -n` namerefs.
   # Listed under the Bash32Compat ratchet as accepted tech debt.
   # Burn-down tracked in t2024 / t2025 / t2026 (per-script follow-ups).
   if [[ -z "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]:-}" ]] || (( BASH_VERSINFO[0] < 4 || (BASH_VERSINFO[0] == 4 && BASH_VERSINFO[1] < 3) )); then
       printf '%s: requires bash 4.3+ (namerefs). Running bash %s.\n' \
           "${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}" "${BASH_VERSION:-unknown}" >&2
       printf 'Install a newer bash with: brew install bash\n' >&2
       exit 1
   fi
   ```

   Apply to:
   - `.agents/scripts/compare-models-helper.sh` — insert after line 30 (`set -euo pipefail`)
   - `.agents/scripts/email-delivery-test-helper.sh` — find the equivalent line and insert immediately after
   - `.agents/scripts/document-creation-helper.sh` — same

5. **Update `reference/bash-compat.md:14`**. Current line:

   ```markdown
   - `${var,,}` / `${var^^}` (case conversion) — use `tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'`
   ```

   Replace with:

   ```markdown
   - Case conversion — use `tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'` (or `tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'`). ALL four forms are bash 4.0+ and will not error on bash 3.2 — they will silently produce the wrong output or emit `bad substitution` at runtime:
     - `${var^^}` — uppercase all
     - `${var,,}` — lowercase all
     - `${var^}` — uppercase first letter (this is the form that caused t17993)
     - `${var,}` — lowercase first letter
   ```

6. **Decrement the ratchet** in `.agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf` if `memory-pressure-monitor.sh:464-465` counts against `BASH32_COMPAT_THRESHOLD`. Verify the count before/after the fix with the existing scanner and adjust the threshold downward by the exact number of violations removed (preserves the burn-down ratchet semantics).

7. **File burn-down follow-ups** as separate tasks (do NOT include in this PR):
   - `t2024 refactor(compare-models): replace local -n namerefs with positional args / temp files` — tier:reasoning, ~6h
   - `t2025 refactor(document-creation): replace local -n namerefs with positional args` — tier:reasoning, ~3h
   - `t2026 refactor(email-delivery-test): replace local -n namerefs with positional args` — tier:standard, ~2h

### Verification

```bash
# 1. Scanner catches the exact t17993 pattern going forward
echo 'x="${foo^}"' > /tmp/bash32-probe.sh
bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --check=bash32 2>&1 | grep -q "single-letter" && echo "OK: scanner catches \${var^}"
rm /tmp/bash32-probe.sh

# 2. memory-pressure-monitor.sh has no remaining case-mod
grep -nE '\$\{[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*[,^][,^]?\}' .agents/scripts/memory-pressure-monitor.sh | grep -v '^[0-9]*:[[:space:]]*#' && echo FAIL || echo OK

# 3. Nameref-heavy scripts fail fast on bash 3.2
/bin/bash -c 'bash .agents/scripts/compare-models-helper.sh help 2>&1 | head -3' # should print "requires bash 4.3+" on Bash 3.2
# (or verify BASH_VERSINFO guard is present in source)
grep -c 'BASH_VERSINFO' .agents/scripts/compare-models-helper.sh .agents/scripts/email-delivery-test-helper.sh .agents/scripts/document-creation-helper.sh

# 4. Doc lists all four case-mod forms
grep -c '\${var\^}' .agents/reference/bash-compat.md
grep -c '\${var,}' .agents/reference/bash-compat.md

# 5. Full linter pass
bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh 2>&1 | tail -30

# 6. CI workflow locally (using act) if available, otherwise just shellcheck
shellcheck .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh .agents/scripts/memory-pressure-monitor.sh .agents/scripts/compare-models-helper.sh
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both `_scan_bash32_file` in `linters-local.sh` and the `bash32-compat` job in `code-quality.yml` flag `${var^}` and `${var,}` when inserted into a test file.
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "printf 'x=\"${foo^}\"\\n' > /tmp/t2023-probe.sh && bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --check=bash32 2>&1 | grep -q 'single-letter' && rm /tmp/t2023-probe.sh"
  ```
- [ ] `memory-pressure-monitor.sh` contains zero `${var,,}` / `${var^^}` / `${var,}` / `${var^}` outside comments.
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "\\$\\{[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*[,\\^][,\\^]?\\}"
    path: ".agents/scripts/memory-pressure-monitor.sh"
    expect: absent
  ```
- [ ] Each of `compare-models-helper.sh`, `email-delivery-test-helper.sh`, `document-creation-helper.sh` has a `BASH_VERSINFO` guard that exits with a readable error on bash 3.2.
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "BASH_VERSINFO"
    path: ".agents/scripts/compare-models-helper.sh"
  ```
- [ ] `reference/bash-compat.md` explicitly lists all four case-mod forms (`${var^}`, `${var,}`, `${var^^}`, `${var,,}`).
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "grep -q '\\${var\\^}' .agents/reference/bash-compat.md && grep -q '\\${var,}' .agents/reference/bash-compat.md"
  ```
- [ ] `BASH32_COMPAT_THRESHOLD` in `complexity-thresholds.conf` is decremented by exactly the number of violations removed, OR stays at 72 if the fixed violations weren't counted (the CI scanner doesn't check `,,}`, so they weren't — document the finding in the PR description).
- [ ] Three follow-up burn-down task entries (t2024, t2025, t2026) exist in TODO.md with brief files.
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "grep -q '^- \\[ \\] t2024' TODO.md && grep -q '^- \\[ \\] t2025' TODO.md && grep -q '^- \\[ \\] t2026' TODO.md"
  ```
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean on all modified files, `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` passes, CI `bash32-compat` job passes.

## Context & Decisions

- **Why not just source `check_bash32_compat` from the CI workflow**: that would be cleaner but requires the CI workflow to source `linters-local.sh`, which pulls in the full linter machinery (cleanup scopes, temp files, other checks). Duplicating the two new regex blocks inline is a 10-line change; the consolidation is worth a separate task (filed inline as a TODO in the workflow comment).
- **Why runtime guards instead of refactoring namerefs now**: `compare-models-helper.sh` alone has 43 nameref uses across functions that are architecturally designed around output parameters. Refactoring to positional args/temp files is a multi-hour rewrite that deserves its own task and its own review. The guard is belt-and-braces: if a user on Bash 3.2 runs the script, they get a clear error in 3 lines instead of `local: -n: not a valid identifier` mid-execution.
- **Why not remove from the ratchet entirely**: the ratchet is doing its job (no *new* namerefs are being added; the count is stable). Adding guards plus burn-down tasks converts "accepted tech debt" into "accepted tech debt with a known exit path", which is the correct posture.
- **Why the single-letter patterns weren't scanned**: historical artefact. The scanner was added in GH#17371 as `"\t"`/`"\n"` detection, extended later with associative arrays and namerefs, and extended again when someone added `,,}` / `^^}` — but only the double forms because those were the documented forms. No one reviewed whether the *regex* matched what the *doc* said.
- **Non-goal**: actually refactoring `compare-models-helper.sh` etc. — that's t2024-t2026.
- **Non-goal**: extending `bash-compat.md` to enforce the other currently-unenforced items (`|&`, negative offsets, `mapfile`). Separate scope; file as follow-up if observed.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh:1221-1268` — `_scan_bash32_file`, the local-mode scanner
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh:1270-1295` — `check_bash32_compat`, the local gate
- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml:72-154` — CI `bash32-compat` job (currently a narrower subset of the local check)
- `.agents/scripts/memory-pressure-monitor.sh:461-469` — the one remaining production-code `${var,,}` block
- `.agents/scripts/compare-models-helper.sh:1017-3000` — nameref usage (43 lines, primary burn-down target)
- `.agents/scripts/document-creation-helper.sh:1509-1625` — nameref usage (11 lines)
- `.agents/scripts/email-delivery-test-helper.sh` — nameref usage (12 lines; exact locations to be determined during implementation)
- `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md:14` — case-conversion doc line that only mentions double forms
- `.agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf` — `BASH32_COMPAT_THRESHOLD=72`
- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-helper.sh:681-683` — reference implementation of the `printf + tr` pattern for case conversion
- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh:365-370` — reference implementation from PR #17994 (the fix that motivated this task)

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** t2024, t2025, t2026 (nameref refactor tasks that should be filed but not dispatched until this lands — the guards added here let the three scripts keep running in the interim)
- **External:** none

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Research/read | 15m | Re-read `_scan_bash32_file`, verify CI workflow structure |
| Scanner regex additions | 30m | Two grep blocks × two files (local + CI); test with probe files |

title: t2024: scope simplification gate on cited line ranges, not file size alone
body:
## Summary

The large-file simplification gate was blocking issues whose bodies cited files for diagnostic **context** rather than as **edit targets**. The fix teaches the gate to distinguish between the two by reading the line qualifier on each cited reference.

## The concrete bug

Issue #18473 (triage JSONL root cause) was tagged `needs-simplification` by the pulse because its body references `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:1477` as context ("this is where opencode is invoked with `--format json`"). The gate treated that reference as if the worker would rewrite the 3123-line file — triggering the gate even though:

- The actual fix lives entirely in `.agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh` (615 lines)
- The edit is a 33-line targeted change at `:221-253`
- The issue body explicitly says `headless-runtime-helper.sh` must NOT change

Pulse log:

```text
[pulse-wrapper] Large-file gate: #18473 in marcusquinn/aidevops targets .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh (3123 lines)
```

## Root cause

The extractor in `_issue_targets_large_files()` at `pulse-dispatch-core.sh:732-747` was stripping the `:NNN` or `:START-END` line qualifier from every file reference via `sed 's/:.*//'`, then running `wc -l` on the bare filename. The line range — the one piece of information needed to distinguish "33-line targeted edit" from "whole-file rewrite" — was thrown away before the gate check.

## Fix

Teach the extractor to preserve line qualifiers and branch on them in the gate loop:

1. **Single-line citations** (`file.sh:1477`) → treat as context references for the human reader. A worker does not "edit line 1477"; it edits a function or a range. Skip these for gate evaluation entirely.

2. **Ranged citations** (`file.sh:221-253`) → if the range size is at most `SCOPED_RANGE_THRESHOLD` (default 300), pass the gate regardless of the enclosing file's total line count. The worker navigates only the cited range.

3. **File-only references** (`file.sh`, no qualifier) → fall through to the existing `wc -l > LARGE_FILE_LINE_THRESHOLD` check. This preserves the gate's original safety for whole-file rewrites.

4. **New env var** `SCOPED_RANGE_THRESHOLD` declared next to `LARGE_FILE_LINE_THRESHOLD` in `pulse-wrapper.sh`, documented with the design rationale.

5. **Explicit log lines** for each decision branch so future debugging is easy:
   - `Large-file gate: #N skipping file.sh:1477 (single-line citation — context reference, not edit target)`
   - `Large-file gate: #N scoped-range pass for file.sh:221-253 (33 lines, threshold 300)`
   - `Large-file gate: #N targets file.sh (3123 lines)` (existing, when file-size check fires)

## Retroactive effect

Once this lands, `_reevaluate_simplification_labels` (t1998) runs on the next pulse cycle and clears any `needs-simplification` label that was applied under the old behaviour on an issue that now passes the new check. #18473 and any similar issues are unblocked automatically — no manual label cleanup.

## Verification

```text
$ shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
→ exit 0 (info-level SC2016 warnings pre-existing, not introduced)

$ bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh
All 26 tests passed

$ # Gate parser sanity test (four cases):
T1 file.sh:1477       → SKIP (single-line context ref)
T2 file.sh:221-253    → PASS (33 lines, scoped)
T3 file.sh:100-500    → FALL-THROUGH (401 > 300)
T4 file.sh            → FALL-THROUGH (no qualifier)
```

## Files changed

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — new `SCOPED_RANGE_THRESHOLD` env var + comment block (~18 lines)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh` — extractor and gate loop (~60 lines changed/added)
- `todo/tasks/t2024-brief.md` — new brief

## Related

- **Companion fix**: #18473 / t2025 — fixes the underlying triage JSONL parsing bug that this task's broken gate was blocking
- **Architectural reference**: t1998 — the re-eval mechanism that will clear stale labels on the next cycle after this lands
- **Origin**: session that produced #18471 (t2014) and the #18473 investigation

Resolves #TBD

title: t2025: fix sandboxed triage JSONL parsing (implementation of #18473)
body:
## Summary

Fix the root cause of 100%-broken sandboxed triage reviews by parsing the JSONL transcript that `opencode run --format json` emits, instead of searching for `## Review:` in the escaped-JSON raw capture.

## The concrete bug

Last successful sandboxed triage in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`: `22991: Posted sandboxed triage review for #17490` — ~106,000 log lines ago. Every triage attempt since has been suppressed by the safety filter as either "raw sandbox output" or "had no review header":

```text
127509: SECURITY: triage review for #18383 was raw sandbox output — suppressed (51480 chars)
129401: SECURITY: triage review for #18429 was raw sandbox output — suppressed (57540 chars)
129407: Triage review for #18428 had no review header — suppressed (72233 chars)
129595: Triage review for #18439 had no review header — suppressed (123252 chars)
129792: Triage review for #18439 had no review header — suppressed (157690 chars)
```

Both failure classes come from the same root cause, just different branches of the safety filter.

## Root cause (two collaborating bugs in one dispatch path)

1. **`pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh` captured with `>"$review_output_file" 2>&1`** — this merged sandbox stderr lines (`[INFO] Executing (timeout=…, network_blocked=…)` from `sandbox-exec-helper.sh:1013`) into the review capture. These match the infra-marker regex and trigger the "raw sandbox output" SECURITY suppression on cycles where they leak.

2. **`headless-runtime-helper.sh:1477` invokes `opencode run … --format json`**, so the capture is JSONL: one JSON object per line covering the user prompt, every tool_use event, every tool_result (which serializes full file contents for Read tool calls), and assistant messages. The `## Review:` header lives inside an escaped JSON string at `.message.content[].text`, so the plain-text extractor `sed -n '/^## .*[Rr]eview/,$ p'` can never match `^##` at column 0 — it returns empty, and the safety filter classifies the whole capture as "no review header".

## Fix

Three changes inside `_dispatch_triage_review_worker()` in `pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh`:

### 1. Separate stderr from stdout capture

```diff
-        --prompt-file "$prefetch_file" </dev/null >"$review_output_file" 2>&1
+        --prompt-file "$prefetch_file" </dev/null >"$review_output_file" 2>"$review_stderr_file"
```

Sandbox INFO lines go to a separate file; the review capture is clean.

### 2. Parse JSONL via jq before the safety filter

Replaces the old `review_text=$(cat "$review_output_file")` with:

```bash
jsonl_parsed=$(jq -rs '
    [.[] | select(.type == "assistant")] as $assistants
    | if ($assistants | length) > 0 then
        $assistants | last | (.message.content // .content // "")
        | if type == "array" then
            [.[] | select(.type == "text") | .text] | join("\n")
          elif type == "string" then
            .
          else
            ""
          end
      else
        ""
      end
' "$review_output_file" 2>/dev/null)
```

- Handles both `.message.content` as an array of content blocks AND as a string (opencode schema has varied)
- Coalesces `.message.content` with `.content` for different opencode versions
- Picks the LAST assistant message (skips intermediate thinking steps)
- Falls through to raw `cat "$review_output_file"` if jq returns empty — same behaviour as before for non-JSONL edge cases (opencode crash, format change)

Then applies the existing `^## .*[Rr]eview` extractor to the parsed plain text, which now matches correctly.

### 3. Save failed captures to a debug directory

New block before `unlock_issue_after_worker`:

- Creates `${TRIAGE_DEBUG_DIR:-~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/triage-debug}` on first failure
- Copies the raw JSONL + a `.meta` sidecar (reason, timestamp, slug, issue number, char count, stderr presence) on every failed triage
- Capped at 100 files (drop oldest to make room) to prevent runaway growth
- Logs the save location

This prevents the next regression from being as invisible as this one.

## Verification

```text
$ shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh
→ exit 0

$ bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh
All 26 tests passed

$ # jq extractor sanity test (four shapes):
Shape 1 (content as array of text blocks)      → returns "## Review: Approved\n..."
Shape 2 (content as string)                     → returns string directly
Shape 3 (multiple assistant messages)           → returns LAST
Shape 4 (non-JSONL garbage)                     → jq fails, raw fallback fires
```

## Why not change `--format json` in `headless-runtime-helper.sh`?

It's load-bearing for every other caller:

- Session DB merge (`_merge_worker_db`) relies on structured output
- `observability-helper.sh:126` parses JSONL for usage/cost/timing telemetry
- The session-miner pulse reads JSONL for cross-session analytics

Changing the flag would break all of these. The fix has to stay localised to the triage dispatch path.

## Files changed

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh` — three edits in `_dispatch_triage_review_worker()` (+90 / -4 lines)
- `todo/tasks/t2025-brief.md` — new brief

## Smoke-test plan (post-merge)

Once this lands and deploys, the next pulse cycle should produce "Posted sandboxed triage review" log entries on any `needs-maintainer-review` issue whose content hash has changed since the last attempt. The `triage-failed` label on stale issues can be cleared with:

```bash
gh issue list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --label triage-failed --state open --json number --jq '.[].number' | while read n; do
  gh issue edit "$n" --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --remove-label triage-failed
  rm -f ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/triage-cache/marcusquinn_aidevops-"$n".{hash,failures}
done
```

## Related

- **Investigation**: #18473 (the root-cause analysis issue this task resolves)
- **Companion fix**: t2024 — scope-aware simplification gate (fixes the systemic mis-gating pattern that initially blocked this PR)
- **Follow-up to**: #18471 (t2014 — cut `TRIAGE_MAX_RETRIES` 3→1), which reduced the observable symptom without fixing the cause

Resolves #18473

title: t2028: feat(gh-wrappers): auto-assign issues created from OWNER interactive sessions
body:
## Summary

`gh_create_issue` in `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh:823` does not auto-assign newly-created issues to the caller, so every interactive session that creates an issue and opens a linked PR hits the maintainer gate's "Issue #N has no assignee" check on first Job 1 run.

## Observed on t2018

During the t2018 `/pr-loop` I created issue #18478 via `gh_create_issue`. The issue was created without an assignee, and when I opened PR #18481 linking it, the `Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` failed with `Issue #18478 has no assignee`. I had to manually run `gh issue edit 18478 --add-assignee marcusquinn` to unblock the gate.

## Root cause

The `claim-task-id.sh` path already has `_auto_assign_issue` (added in t1970), but the direct `gh_create_issue` wrapper never got the same treatment. Two separate issue-creation paths, only one fixed.

## Fix

Mirror the t1970 auto-assign pattern into `gh_create_issue`. Two new helpers in `shared-constants.sh`:

- `_gh_wrapper_args_have_assignee` — detects caller-supplied `--assignee` in any supported form
- `_gh_wrapper_auto_assignee` — returns the appropriate assignee: `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_USER` env override first (t1984 compat), then `gh api user`; empty string for worker origin

`gh_create_issue` calls both helpers and conditionally appends `--assignee <user>` when the session is interactive AND the caller did not pass an explicit `--assignee`.

Worker-origin sessions are unaffected (they still follow their own dispatch flow). Caller-supplied `--assignee` is respected (the wrapper detects it and skips auto-assignment).

## Task

- Brief: `todo/tasks/t2028-brief.md`

title: t2032: fix(pulse-merge): tighten deterministic merge-pass close-comment wording (GH#17574)
body:
## Summary

The deterministic merge-pass close-comment in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh::_close_conflicting_pr()` currently says:

> The work for this task (`tNNN`) has already been committed **directly** to main, so no re-attempt is needed.

This is misleading in the common case where the work landed via a merged sibling PR. Concrete example observed in PR #18486 (closed 2026-04-13T00:42:32Z): the comment claimed "committed directly to main" when the work had actually landed via the squash-merge of sibling PR #18480 merged 1m46s earlier.

## Fix

1. Rewrite the comment template to say `has already landed on main` (unconditional) and append `(via PR #NNN)` only when the matching commit has a squash-merge `(#NNN)` suffix.

title: t2031: fix(pulse-dep-graph): respect non-dep blocks when auto-unblocking
body:
**Task ID:** `t2031` | **Status:** in-progress | **Estimate:** `~45m`
**Logged:** 2026-04-13
**Tags:** `bug` `pulse` `dep-graph` `interactive`

## Summary

`pulse-dep-graph.sh:refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` blindly removes `status:blocked` from any issue whose `blocked-by:` chain has resolved — regardless of *why* the label was applied. This wastes cycles on issues blocked for non-dep reasons (worker BLOCKED exits, watchdog thrash kills, terminal blockers, manual human holds) by re-queuing them into guaranteed re-BLOCKED dispatches.

## Real-world case

`<webapp>#2273` (`t222: Build MCP server adapter`). On 2026-04-11 a worker exited BLOCKED citing THREE reasons: (1) open `blocked-by:t215,t219,t220` chain, (2) the issue body's explicit defer gate (`Defer until Phase 1-6 are working end-to-end @alexey`), (3) missing implementation context. It applied `status:blocked`. Two days later the pulse's `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` removed the label because the dep chain had resolved (all three blockers closed). Fresh workers were dispatched and had to exit BLOCKED again.

## Root cause

`refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` assumes every `status:blocked` label means "blocked because of open deps". That assumption is false. The label is also applied by:

1. `pulse-dispatch-core.sh:1425` (`_apply_terminal_blocker`) — token scope issues, ACTION REQUIRED comments.
2. `worker-watchdog.sh:872` — zero-commit thrash kills.
3. Worker sessions themselves — exiting BLOCKED with structured evidence comments.
4. Human operators — manual holds in response to defer gates in issue bodies.

None of these are resolved by closing the dep chain. The refresh routine has no provenance check.

## Fix (landing in this PR)

Two new signals guard the unblock edit:

1. **Body defer marker cached at build time** — `build_dependency_graph_cache` scans the issue body for `defer until`, `do not dispatch`, `on hold`, `paused`, `hold for`, `HUMAN_UNBLOCK_REQUIRED` and records a `has_defer_marker` boolean per blocked_by entry (plus a top-level `defer_flags` map).
2. **Non-dep BLOCKED markers in recent comments** — before removing the label, the refresh fetches the 10 most recent comments and checks for `**BLOCKED** ... cannot proceed` (worker exit), `Worker Watchdog Kill`, `Terminal blocker detected`, `ACTION REQUIRED`, `HUMAN_UNBLOCK_REQUIRED`.

If either signal fires, the refresh logs `NOT unblocking #N in SLUG — non-dep block detected (body-defer|comment-marker)` and leaves the label in place. Only when both signals are clean AND the blocked-by chain has resolved does it unblock.

Conservative-by-default: a false positive (leaving an issue blocked that could be unblocked) costs nothing — a human re-queues. A false negative (unblocking an issue that should stay blocked) costs a worker session and context window each time.

## Worker Guidance (interactive self-implementation)

**Files to modify:**

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` — add defer-flag extraction in `build_dependency_graph_cache`, add `_should_defer_auto_unblock` helper, gate the unblock edit in `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph`.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-non-dep-block.sh` — 31 assertions covering body markers, comment markers, and the integrated helper via a mocked `gh` stub.

**Reference patterns:**

- Parse approach models on the existing blocked-by parse at `pulse-dep-graph.sh:134-141` (two-step grep, POSIX classes).
- Test harness models on `tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-parse.sh`.
- Wrapper usage: `gh_create_issue` / `gh_create_pr` from `shared-constants.sh:823` (origin labels).

**Verification:**

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-non-dep-block.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-non-dep-block.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-parse.sh
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build_dependency_graph_cache` records `has_defer_marker` per `blocked_by` entry and populates a top-level `defer_flags` map.
- [ ] `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` skips unblock when body or comment markers indicate non-dep block.
- [ ] New regression test passes (31 assertions across 3 groups).
- [ ] `shellcheck` passes on both files.
- [ ] Existing `test-pulse-dep-graph-parse.sh` still passes (no regression).

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Related:** `t1935` (the t2031 hardening target), `t2015` (the sibling fix that reworked the body parse)

title: t2029: fix(issue-sync): make sync-on-pr-merge push failure visible instead of silent
body:
## Summary

The `sync-on-pr-merge` job in `issue-sync.yml:288-515` has been silently failing for ~3 weeks. It DOES try to auto-mark TODO entries complete on PR merge, but the `git push` is rejected by branch protection and the retry loop has no `exit 1` after failure — so the workflow reports SUCCESS even though TODO.md was never updated.

## Observed

- Last successful GA `chore: mark tNNN complete` commit: **2026-03-20** (3 weeks ago).
- During t2015/t2018 /pr-loop flows I ran `task-complete-helper.sh` manually, assuming the bot path was broken.
- Investigation showed the push is rejected with `GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/main` because `github-actions[bot]` cannot bypass `required_approving_review_count: 1`.

## Root cause

Classic branch protection on personal-account public repos does not support `bypass_pull_request_allowances` — confirmed HTTP 500 on direct PATCH API call. The real fix options are both non-trivial:

1. **Migrate to GitHub Rulesets** (~2-3h): rulesets support `bypass_actors` for GitHub Apps on personal repos. Medium risk, replicates existing rules.
2. **Fine-grained PAT** (~30m + ongoing rotation): store admin-bypass PAT as secret.

## Scope of THIS fix

Make the failure LOUD instead of silent. 15 minutes, zero risk.

- Track push success explicitly via `PUSH_SUCCEEDED` variable
- On failure: `::error::` workflow message + `exit 1` + PR comment with exact `task-complete-helper.sh` manual command
- Document the limitation in `.agents/AGENTS.md`
- File a follow-up task for the real fix

Future PR merges that hit the branch-protection wall will show a failed workflow step and a comment on the merged PR with the exact command to run. No more silent accumulation.

## Task

- Task ID: `t2029`
- Brief: `todo/tasks/t2029-brief.md`
- Tier: `tier:simple`
- Estimate: ~15m

title: bug(maintainer-gate): origin:interactive auto-pass only fires for PRs with no linked issues
body:
## Summary

`.github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml` has an `origin:interactive` auto-pass at line 177 that only fires inside the `if [[ -z "$LINKED_ISSUES" ]]` block — i.e., only for PRs that have NO linked issues. For PRs with linked issues (which is **every well-formed PR** that uses `Resolves #NNN`), the check is skipped entirely and the linked-issue loop at line 219 can block on "no assignee" even when the PR author is the repo OWNER and the PR carries `origin:interactive`.

This creates a workflow dead-end where legitimate maintainer-interactive work is blocked by the framework's own branch protection.

## Evidence from this session

Four PRs opened during an interactive maintainer session tonight (#18472, #18480, #18497, #18498) all hit the same blocker:

```text
$ gh pr view 18497 --json mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision
mergeState=BLOCKED reviewDecision=REVIEW_REQUIRED
```

Root cause traced to `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml:275-289`:

```bash
if [[ -z "$ASSIGNEES" ]]; then
  PR_AUTHOR_IS_MAINTAINER=false
  if [[ "$PR_AUTHOR_ASSOCIATION" == "OWNER" ]] || \
     [[ "$PR_AUTHOR_ASSOCIATION" == "MEMBER" ]]; then
    PR_AUTHOR_IS_MAINTAINER=true
  fi

  if [[ "$ISSUE_AUTHOR" == "github-actions[bot]" ]] && [[ "$PR_AUTHOR_IS_MAINTAINER" == "true" ]]; then
    echo "EXEMPT: ..."
  else
    BLOCKED=true
    REASONS="${REASONS}Issue #${ISSUE_NUM} has no assignee..."
  fi
fi
```

The exemption requires BOTH:
1. Issue author is `github-actions[bot]`
2. PR author is OWNER/MEMBER

Issues created manually via `gh issue create` (which is what happens when `claim-task-id.sh`'s issue-sync fallback path kicks in) have the human author, not the bot. So the exemption never fires for human-authored issues — even when the PR has `origin:interactive` and the PR author is the OWNER.

## Proposed fix

Add a second exemption branch for `origin:interactive` + OWNER/MEMBER at the "no assignee" check. Replace:

```bash
if [[ "$ISSUE_AUTHOR" == "github-actions[bot]" ]] && [[ "$PR_AUTHOR_IS_MAINTAINER" == "true" ]]; then
  echo "EXEMPT: Issue #$ISSUE_NUM created by github-actions[bot] and PR author is maintainer (OWNER/MEMBER) — assignee check skipped"
else
  BLOCKED=true
  ...
```

With:

```bash
if [[ "$ISSUE_AUTHOR" == "github-actions[bot]" ]] && [[ "$PR_AUTHOR_IS_MAINTAINER" == "true" ]]; then
  echo "EXEMPT: Issue #$ISSUE_NUM created by github-actions[bot] and PR author is maintainer — assignee check skipped"
elif echo "$PR_LABELS" | grep -q 'origin:interactive' && [[ "$PR_AUTHOR_IS_MAINTAINER" == "true" ]]; then
  echo "EXEMPT: PR has origin:interactive and author is maintainer (${PR_AUTHOR_ASSOCIATION}) — assignee check bypassed (matches the no-linked-issues origin:interactive auto-pass at line 177)"
else
  BLOCKED=true
  ...
```

**Same change in the `retrigger-pr-checks` job** (around line 600), which has its own copy of the linked-issue loop for issue-event re-triggers.

## Security

The `origin:interactive` label is NOT protected (`origin:worker` is), so a contributor could theoretically apply it manually. That's why the exemption must also check `PR_AUTHOR_ASSOCIATION == OWNER || MEMBER` — same guard as the existing line-177 bypass. COLLABORATOR is explicitly excluded. This matches the security model documented in `.agents/AGENTS.md` under "`origin:interactive` implies maintainer approval".

## Why this can't be auto-dispatched

This is a CI workflow change that gates ALL dispatched workers. If the fix has a bug, headless workers get stuck behind the very gate this edits. **It should be reviewed and merged interactively by the maintainer** with full awareness of the blast radius. Tag: `needs-maintainer-review`, not `auto-dispatch`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `origin:interactive` + OWNER/MEMBER exempts the "no assignee" check in the `check-pr` job
- [ ] Same exemption applied in the `retrigger-pr-checks` job
- [ ] A fresh origin:interactive PR by the maintainer with a linked unassigned issue no longer reports `REVIEW_REQUIRED` on `mergeStateStatus`
- [ ] Existing exemption for `github-actions[bot]` issues still works unchanged
- [ ] Existing block for COLLABORATOR-authored PRs with origin:interactive still fires

## Related

- Discovered while investigating why PRs #18472, #18480, #18497 (all origin:interactive, all by OWNER) kept getting blocked tonight
- Related to #18285 (the original origin:interactive maintainer-approval gate) and GH#18334 (the original implementation)

title: meta: propagate Section 0 discovery discipline from review to implementation (build.txt / build+ agent)
body:
## Summary

t2017 / PR #18480 taught the `/review-issue-pr` workflow agent to run a "Section 0 Pre-Review Discovery" before accepting proposed fixes — specifically the temporal-duplicate check (`git log --since="<issue date>"` + `gh pr list --state merged --search "<keywords>"`) that catches proposals for problems already solved by recently-merged work.

**The same discipline needs to apply to implementation, not just review.** This task propagates the Section 0 checks into the pre-implementation workflow so autonomous coding sessions (interactive or headless) run the same discovery before writing code.

## The concrete failure this is meant to prevent

During the session that produced this task (and PR #18480 / t2017 itself), the model:

1. Investigated a reported triage bug and filed #18473 with a root-cause analysis based on pulse log entries from ~4 hours earlier
2. Claimed task t2025 and implemented a JSON-parsing fix in `pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh`
3. Opened PR #18498 with the fix

Then, while rebasing the PR, discovered that **commit `a084f425f` (t2019 / PR #18491) had merged 2 hours earlier and fixed the same bug more thoroughly** — and was already deployed to the running pulse (file mtime 02:09, investigation began after 02:09).

The model had just spent ~30 minutes writing a duplicate fix for a bug that was already fixed. The cost:

- ~30 minutes of model time
- Full workflow: task ID claim + worktree + brief + commit + push + issue + PR
- Closing the duplicate with a forensic explanation

The duplicate would have been caught by ONE command before starting:

```bash
git log --since="6 hours ago" --oneline -- .agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh
```

Which would have surfaced `a084f425f t2019: fix(pulse-triage): parse JSON output + inline prompt + shape validation (#18491)` as a commit on the exact file I was about to modify, with keywords matching my proposed fix. Exactly the pattern t2017's Section 0.1 (Pre-Review Discovery → Duplicate and temporal-duplicate check) was designed to catch — and the model wrote that discipline earlier in the same session, then failed to apply it to itself 90 minutes later.

## What to change

### Option A: extend `prompts/build.txt` with a "Pre-implementation discovery" rule

In `.agents/prompts/build.txt` under the existing "Completion and quality discipline" section, add a short paragraph:

```markdown
# Pre-implementation discovery (MANDATORY for non-trivial changes)
Before writing code for any non-trivial task — whether in response to an issue,
a brief, or a user request — run the Section 0 discovery checks from
workflows/review-issue-pr.md against yourself:
- `git log --since="<issue date or 24h ago>" --oneline -- <affected files>` — look for recent commits that may have already fixed the same bug
- `gh pr list --state merged --search "<keywords>" --limit 10` — look for in-flight or recently-merged work that supersedes the task
- `git log --since="1 day ago" --grep="<keywords>"` — look for related work across the whole repo
If any check returns a plausible match, STOP and verify whether the work is
already done. A duplicate fix is worse than doing nothing: it wastes tokens,
pollutes the timeline, and may regress a correct fix landed elsewhere.
```

### Option B: extend `workflows/build.md` (or equivalent build+ entry) with a discovery preamble

Add a numbered step "0. Pre-implementation discovery" that mirrors review-issue-pr.md Section 0 but is worded for the implementation side.

### Option C: both — the rule in `build.txt` for universal prompt-level enforcement AND a reference in `build.md` / full-loop docs for workflow visibility.

Option C is recommended. `build.txt` is always in context; `build.md`-level docs get read when workflows are followed.

## Scope caveat

**This is a prompt/instruction change**, not a code change. It belongs in an interactive PR reviewed with awareness that it affects every future agent session. Not suitable for auto-dispatch — a worker dispatched to edit its own system prompt is a recursive footgun. Tag: `needs-maintainer-review`, not `auto-dispatch`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `prompts/build.txt` contains a "Pre-implementation discovery" rule that references the same checks as `workflows/review-issue-pr.md` Section 0.1
- [ ] A brief mentioning the rule is added to the "Completion and quality discipline" section so the rule is discoverable by the self-assessment protocol
- [ ] Optional: a reciprocal reference is added to `workflows/review-issue-pr.md` Section 0 explaining that the same discipline applies at implementation time

## Why this matters beyond the one failure above

The specific failure this prevents — duplicating a fix that just landed — has a small direct cost per incident (~30 min + one duplicate PR). But it's symptomatic of a deeper pattern: autonomous coders tend to treat the codebase as frozen at the moment they read it, rather than as a living system where other work may have landed since the prompt was loaded. The Section 0 discipline is a small, cheap habit that rewards disproportionately: it catches not just duplicates, but also:

- Fixes that would regress recently-added invariants (the "my cache would defeat t1998" scenario from the same session)
- Proposals misframed against codebase reality (e.g., citing line numbers that drifted after a refactor)
- Work already in flight (open PRs on the same file) where coordination is better than collision

t2017 baked this into the REVIEWER role. This task bakes it into the IMPLEMENTER role. They're the same discipline; they need to live in both places.

## Related

- **Baked this into review**: #18480 (t2017)
- **The failure that prompted this task**: #18498 close comment (t2025 duplicate-discovery post-mortem)
- **The fix that was duplicated**: #18491 (t2019)

${SIG}

title: fix(deploy): opencode agent stub grants bash:true and external_directory:allow — more permissive than source
body:
## Problem

The deployed OpenCode agent stub at `~/.config/opencode/agent/triage-review.md` is a 305-byte pointer that grants **more tools than the source agent file** it claims to reference. This was discovered during the t2019 / PR #18491 investigation (see pulse-wrapper.log evidence for #18428).

**Deployed stub** (`~/.config/opencode/agent/triage-review.md`):

```yaml
---
description: Read ~/.aidevops/agents/workflows/triage-review.md
mode: subagent
temperature: 0.2
permission:
  external_directory: allow   # <-- grants access beyond the work dir
tools:
  read: true
  bash: true                  # <-- grants Bash execution
---
```

**Source file** (`.agents/workflows/triage-review.md`, after t2019 hardening):

```yaml
---
description: Sandboxed triage review for external contributor issues — zero network access
model: opus
mode: subagent
temperature: 0.2
tools:
  read: true
  write: false
  edit: false
  bash: false                 # <-- Bash explicitly denied
  glob: true
  grep: true
  webfetch: false
  task: false
---
```

Two concrete discrepancies:

1. **`bash: true` vs `bash: false`** — the stub grants shell execution; the source denies it.
2. **`external_directory: allow`** — the stub grants filesystem access beyond the work directory; the source has no such grant.

## Why this matters (residual risk)

t2019 / PR #18491 shipped a prompt-level fix that tells the model "DO NOT use Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write, Edit, or any other tools. ALL context you need is in this prompt." A well-aligned model follows this regardless of what tools the runtime grants. But this is defence-in-depth, not a hard boundary:

- A prompt-injected issue body (the exact adversarial case triage-review exists to handle) could try to override the "no tools" instruction. If the model yields, the stub's `bash: true` becomes the attack surface.
- Off-distribution models, new model releases, or model regressions could drift on prompt adherence.
- The YAML-level tool restriction is the runtime-enforced boundary; the prompt-level rule is a request.

The stub was presumably generated by a deployment script that coded the permissive tools, not by copying the source file. This is a tooling / deployment bug.

## What to investigate

1. **Where does the stub get generated?** `.agents/workflows/triage-review.md` is the source; the stub lives at `~/.config/opencode/agent/triage-review.md`. Something writes the stub — it is not a direct copy. Likely candidates:
   - `setup.sh` or one of its subscripts (no match for `triage-review` in `setup.sh`, needs deeper scan)
   - `generate-opencode-agents.sh` (if it exists — see post-release sync in `version-manager.sh`)
   - A manual one-off script that was never removed
2. **Audit other workflow agents deployed to `~/.config/opencode/agent/`.** If triage-review is a pointer-stub, other sandboxed agents may have the same pattern (review-issue-pr, etc.) and the same over-permissioning.
3. **Audit Claude Code agent deployments.** No `triage-review.md` exists under `~/.claude/agents/` — the whole Claude CLI path was relying on the default `build-plus` fallback. Confirm whether Claude CLI sandboxed agents are supposed to live under `~/.claude/agents/` and, if so, whether the deployment is missing entirely or has a different structure.

## Proposed fix

The simplest correct deployment is: copy the source `.agents/workflows/triage-review.md` (with its full body and restrictive tool declarations) directly to `~/.config/opencode/agent/triage-review.md` rather than writing a pointer stub. No "MANDATORY: first action is read…" trick needed — the agent file body IS the instructions.

- EDIT or add to a deployment script (likely `setup.sh` or a helper it calls): replace the pointer-stub generation with a direct copy.
- EDIT: ensure the copied file's YAML frontmatter matches the source (`bash: false`, no `external_directory: allow`, full `glob`/`grep`/`webfetch`/`task` restrictions).
- NEW (optional): extend `generate-opencode-agents.sh` (if it exists) to emit a CI-style validation check that compares every deployed file's YAML frontmatter to its source and fails if they diverge.

## Verification

```bash
# After fix — the deployed file should have bash:false and the full rule body
grep -E 'bash:|external_directory' ~/.config/opencode/agent/triage-review.md
# Expected: "bash: false", no "external_directory" line

# Full source ↔ deployed parity
diff -u ~/Git/aidevops/.agents/workflows/triage-review.md ~/.config/opencode/agent/triage-review.md
# Expected: empty diff (or only trailing newline / SPDX header whitespace)
```

## Reference pattern

The fix should model on whatever script `version-manager.sh` calls in the "Running post-release aidevops agent sync" step — that is where the stub is (mis)generated today. Reading that script will identify the exact generator and tell you whether to fix the generator or bypass it for restricted-tool agents.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deployed `~/.config/opencode/agent/triage-review.md` has `bash: false`
- [ ] Deployed file has no `external_directory: allow` grant
- [ ] Deployed file's tool list matches the source file (the full `glob/grep/write/edit/webfetch/task` set)
- [ ] An audit script or CI check compares deployed agent frontmatter against source for all sandboxed agents (or at least `triage-review`)
- [ ] t2019 tests (`test-triage-output-shape.sh`, `test-triage-failure-escalation.sh`) still pass

## Context & decisions

- This is a **follow-up to t2019 / #18482 / PR #18491**, not a blocker — the t2019 prompt-level fix is shipped in v3.7.4 and works regardless of this discrepancy.
- Do NOT widen the t2019 fix to inline-patch the stub from the main flow — that conflates the primary fix with deployment hygiene. Keep this issue scoped to "deployment path writes wrong YAML".
- The finding was surfaced during investigation of pulse-wrapper.log for #18428 (three suppressed attempts at 72K / 80K / 62K chars on 2026-04-12); while diagnosing the JSON-extraction root cause, the investigator noticed the stub was permissive and flagged it for a separate task. See `todo/tasks/t2019-brief.md` and PR #18491's smoke-test comment for full context.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — single file deployment fix, requires understanding the deploy script, but no novel design. Narrative brief is sufficient.

title: t2030: refactor(maintainer-gate): move Check -1 out of the empty-linked-issues branch
body:
## Summary

Documented-vs-implemented mismatch in `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml`. `build.txt` says `origin:interactive` PRs from OWNER/MEMBER "pass the maintainer gate automatically, no separate sudo approval needed", but the implementation nests Check -1 inside `if [[ -z "$LINKED_ISSUES" ]]`, so the exemption only fires for PRs with no linked issues. The common case — maintainer opens an interactive PR linking an externally-reported bug — still hits the full linked-issue gate.

## Observed on t2015 this session

1. PR #18474 opened, `origin:interactive`, author OWNER, linked to externally-reported #18429 via `Resolves #18429`.
2. Gate ran, Check -1 skipped because `LINKED_ISSUES=18429` (not empty).
3. Gate blocked on `Issue #18429 has needs-maintainer-review`.
4. User ran `sudo aidevops approve issue 18429` (~30s + sudo prompt + context switch).
5. Gate re-ran via t2018 and passed.

With this fix, steps 3–5 are eliminated.

## Fix

Move Check -1 (lines 164-191 of current maintainer-gate.yml) OUT of the `if [[ -z "$LINKED_ISSUES" ]]` branch. Place it immediately BEFORE that branch so it applies to all PRs regardless of whether they have linked issues.

The security boundary is preserved: `PR_AUTHOR_ASSOCIATION == OWNER/MEMBER` check stays exactly as-is. COLLABORATOR PRs still fall through to the full gate. Only the maintainer-authored case is affected.

## Task

- Task ID: `t2030`
- Brief: `todo/tasks/t2030-brief.md`
- Tier: `tier:simple` (mechanical lexical move, no logic change)
- Estimate: ~15m

## Non-goals

- Job 3 refactor (G3 — tracked separately)
- Moving Check -1 above Check 0 (PR-level NMR)

title: t2034: fix(issue-sync): add GH_TOKEN to Update TODO.md proof-log step
body:
## Summary

Direct follow-up to t2029 (#18506). t2029 added a `gh pr comment` fallback to the `Update TODO.md proof-log` step in `issue-sync.yml` so users see a comment on the merged PR when the auto-completion push is rejected by branch protection. When t2029's own merge ran, the workflow `::error::` messages fired correctly but the `gh pr comment` call **silently failed** because the step's env block doesn't set `GH_TOKEN`.

## Verified observation

```diff
           TASK_ID: ${{ steps.extract.outputs.task_id }}
```

```bash
# Canonical ordered list of mutually-exclusive status:* labels.

#######################################
# Transition an issue to a status:* label atomically.
#

# Returns:
#   0 on gh success, non-zero on gh failure. Errors are suppressed (2>/dev/null)
#   to match existing call-site conventions — callers should not depend on
#   specific exit codes.
#######################################
set_issue_status() {
    local issue_num="$1"
    local repo_slug="$2"
    local new_status="$3"
    shift 3

    # Validate target status (empty is allowed = clear only)
    if [[ -n "$new_status" ]]; then
        local _valid=0
        local _status
        for _status in "${ISSUE_STATUS_LABELS[@]}"; do
            [[ "$_status" == "$new_status" ]] && { _valid=1; break; }

    # a non-fatal 404 that gh swallows. This lets us unconditionally remove
    # all siblings without first querying the issue's current labels.

        else
            _flags+=(--remove-label "status:${_label}")
        fi
    done

    # (e.g., --add-assignee, --remove-assignee, --add-label "other-non-status-label")
    _flags+=("$@")

    gh issue edit "$issue_num" --repo "$repo_slug" "${_flags[@]}" 2>/dev/null
}
```

## Description

Currently affecting seven open `origin:interactive` PRs across this and prior sessions (#18460, #18495, #18497, #18500, #18502, #18505, #18506). Fix: add a new `_gh_auto_assign_from_url` helper in `shared-constants.sh` that parses the URL `gh issue create` echoes, extracts owner/repo/number, and runs `gh issue edit ... --add-assignee <current-user>`. Call it from `gh_create_issue` ONLY when origin is `interactive` (workers continue to skip self-assignment so the dispatcher's deferred assignment logic isn't disturbed). Non-blocking on assignment failure. Verbatim diff in brief, mirror of `claim-task-id.sh:_auto_assign_issue` pattern.

## Worker Guidance

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh:823-829` — replace `gh_create_issue` body with the variant above

### `_gh_auto_assign_from_url` implementation (verbatim)

```bash
# Internal: parse a GitHub issue URL and self-assign to the current user.
# Used by gh_create_issue for origin:interactive sessions so the issue
# matches the maintainer-gate "assigned" check from creation onwards.
# Non-blocking — assignment failure is logged but does not fail the caller.
# URL format: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<num>
_gh_auto_assign_from_url() {
    local issue_url="$1"
    [[ -z "$issue_url" ]] && return 0

    # Parse URL → owner/repo and issue number
    local issue_num repo_slug
    issue_num=$(printf '%s' "$issue_url" | grep -oE '[0-9]+$' || echo "")
    repo_slug=$(printf '%s' "$issue_url" | sed -n 's|^https://github\.com/\([^/]*/[^/]*\)/issues/.*|\1|p')
    [[ -z "$issue_num" || -z "$repo_slug" ]] && return 0

    local current_user
    current_user=$(gh api user --jq '.login' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    [[ -z "$current_user" ]] && return 0

    gh issue edit "$issue_num" --repo "$repo_slug" \
        --add-assignee "$current_user" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    return 0
}
```

# t2035: auto-assign interactive issues in gh_create_issue wrapper

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-04-13
- **Session:** claude-code (interactive)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (session that produced t2014/t2017/t2024 + #18507/#18508)
- **Parent task:** none
- **Conversation context:** While investigating why seven `origin:interactive` PRs were stuck in `BLOCKED/REVIEW_REQUIRED`, traced the cascade to `maintainer-gate.yml`'s "no assignee" check at line 275-289. Filed #18507 to fix the framework gate, but discovered the upstream cause: every issue I created in the session was unassigned because manual `gh issue create` calls (which I was making instead of using the wrapper) never set `--assignee @me`. Even the wrapper `gh_create_issue` in `shared-constants.sh` doesn't auto-assign — only the bare `claim-task-id.sh` fallback path has self-assignment, and only after delegated success. Fixing the wrapper closes the upstream hole and reduces #18507's blast radius.

## What

Make `gh_create_issue` in `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` automatically assign newly-created issues to the current GitHub user when the session origin is `interactive`. Mirror the existing `_auto_assign_issue` pattern from `claim-task-id.sh:607-625`. Worker-origin issues are intentionally NOT auto-assigned — the dispatcher handles their assignment downstream.

The wrapper currently:

```bash
gh_create_issue() {
    local origin_label
    origin_label=$(session_origin_label)
    _ensure_origin_labels_for_args "$@"
    gh issue create "$@" --label "$origin_label"
}
```

Will become:

```bash
gh_create_issue() {
    local origin_label
    origin_label=$(session_origin_label)
    _ensure_origin_labels_for_args "$@"

    # Capture the URL so we can self-assign post-creation
    local issue_url
    if ! issue_url=$(gh issue create "$@" --label "$origin_label" 2>&1); then
        printf '%s\n' "$issue_url" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    # Echo URL to stdout for callers that capture output (matches raw gh behaviour)
    printf '%s\n' "$issue_url"

    # Auto-assign interactive issues. Workers skip this — the dispatcher
    # assigns them downstream, and a self-assignment here would race the
    # dedup guard. Non-blocking: assignment failure does not fail creation.
    if [[ "$origin_label" == "origin:interactive" ]]; then
        _gh_auto_assign_from_url "$issue_url" || true
    fi
    return 0
}
```

Plus a new helper `_gh_auto_assign_from_url` that parses `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<num>` and runs `gh issue edit <num> --repo <owner>/<repo> --add-assignee @me`. Pattern lifted from `claim-task-id.sh:_auto_assign_issue` but driven from a URL instead of (issue_num, repo_path).

## Why

### Direct evidence from the session that produced this brief

Seven `origin:interactive` PRs across multiple sessions were stuck in `BLOCKED/REVIEW_REQUIRED`:

```text
#18460 t2013 — headless-runtime-helper split (pre-existing session)
#18495 t2027 — pr-loop Gate Failure Playbook
#18497 t2024 — scope-aware simplification gate (this session)
#18500 t2028 — auto-assign from interactive sessions (related work)
#18502 t2032 — tighten pulse merge-pass close-comment wording
#18505 t2031 — pulse-dep-graph non-dep blocks
#18506 t2029 — issue-sync push failure visibility
```

Every one was authored by the OWNER, every one carried `origin:interactive`, and every one was blocked because its linked issue had no assignee — which meant the maintainer-gate workflow couldn't apply the OWNER-author exemption.

`#18507` files the workflow-side fix (the gate should also exempt origin:interactive + OWNER for the assignee check). This task is the upstream complement: prevent the unassigned state from existing in the first place.

### Why this is a wrapper-level fix and not a "remember to pass --assignee" prompt rule

`AGENTS.md` already says "NEVER use raw `gh pr create` or `gh issue create` directly. Always use the wrappers". The wrapper is the contract. If the contract is "use the wrapper and the right thing happens", the wrapper has to actually do the right thing — including self-assignment for interactive sessions. A prompt rule telling implementers to "remember to pass --assignee" is fragile and exactly the kind of thing the wrapper exists to prevent.

### Effect

- Eliminates the cascade of unassigned issues that #18507 currently has to work around
- Six of seven currently-stuck PRs (#18460 has additional merge conflicts) become unblockable as soon as the wrapper change deploys
- Zero impact on worker dispatch — the wrapper distinguishes `origin:interactive` from `origin:worker` and only self-assigns the former

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `gh_create_issue` calls `_gh_auto_assign_from_url` after a successful create when the session origin is `interactive`

## Context & Decisions

- **Why post-creation, not via `--assignee` flag on the `gh issue create` call?** Because `--assignee` requires the user to already exist as a collaborator on the repo and silently fails if not — whereas `gh issue edit --add-assignee @me` is more tolerant and gives a clearer error path. - **Why echo the URL to stdout in addition to triggering the helper?** Backwards compatibility: callers that capture `URL=$(gh_create_issue ...)` continue to work. The current `gh issue create` returns the URL on stdout, and the wrapper must preserve that contract.
- **Non-goals:**

# t2036: add deployed-vs-source diagnostic rule to build.txt for runtime investigations

## Origin

- **Session:** claude-code (interactive)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (session that produced t2014/t2017/t2024 + #18473 post-mortem)
- **Parent task:** none (sibling to #18508)
- **Conversation context:** During the same session that produced #18508 (Section 0 discovery discipline for implementation), a related but distinct failure surfaced: when investigating runtime pulse behaviour for #18473, the model read the source file in `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh` and reasoned about what the running pulse was doing — but the deployed copy at `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh` was a NEWER version (mtime 02:09) than the log entries being investigated (timestamps 23:xx). The bug had already been fixed by t2019 / commit `a084f425f` and deployed before the investigation began. Reading source-as-truth led to a multi-hour mis-investigation and a duplicate fix attempt that had to be closed.

This is adjacent to #18508 ("check git log before implementing") but distinct: that rule catches duplicates BEFORE writing code; this rule catches stale-symptom investigations BEFORE writing the wrong analysis. Different failure modes, different fixes, both belong in the harness.

## What

Add a short, concrete diagnostic rule to `.agents/prompts/build.txt` that requires runtime investigations of pulse, agent, or worker behaviour to first establish the deployed-vs-source state of the relevant scripts before reading source code as a model of "what's running". The rule applies whenever an investigation is rooted in runtime artifacts (logs, observed timeouts, failed dispatches, suppressed comments, etc.) where the symptom may have been produced by a previously-deployed version.

The rule belongs in the existing "Error Prevention (top recurring patterns)" section of `build.txt` as a numbered entry — that section already houses similar diagnostic rules and is referenced from the system prompt's quality discipline pointers.

### Proposed text (verbatim, ~14 lines added)

```markdown
# 9. Stale-symptom investigations (runtime debugging)
# When investigating pulse, agent, or worker runtime behaviour reported via
# logs, timeouts, or failed dispatches, the deployed copy at
# `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/<file>` may differ from the source in
# `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/<file>`. The pulse process executes
# DEPLOYED code; investigations that read source-as-truth can spend hours
# analysing a bug that was already fixed and deployed before the
# investigated symptoms occurred.
- Before reading source for runtime investigation: run
  `stat -f '%Sm' ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/<file>` and compare to
  `git -C ~/Git/aidevops log -1 --format='%ai' -- .agents/scripts/<file>`.
  If they differ, identify whether you're reading the deployed version,
  the in-flight source, or somewhere between.
- When the symptom timestamps in logs predate the deployed file mtime,
  treat the symptom as historical — it reflects pre-deploy behaviour.
  Verify the symptom still reproduces against the current deploy before
  filing an investigation issue.
- Source-only debugging is fine for design questions, refactoring,
  and writing new code. The rule applies specifically to runtime
  diagnostics.
- Related discipline: section 7 (Pre-implementation discovery, t2036's
  sibling #18508) covers the complementary case — checking git log for
  recently-merged fixes before WRITING new code.
```

The numbering (`# 9.`) is illustrative — the actual number should follow whatever's currently the next free slot in the "Error Prevention" section at write time.

## Why

### Direct evidence from the session that produced this brief

The triage JSONL bug (#18473) was already fixed by commit `a084f425f` (t2019, PR #18491) which merged at 02:03 UTC and was deployed at 02:09 (verified post-failure via `stat -f '%Sm' ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh`). The investigation that produced #18473 began after 02:09 but read pulse log entries from 23:xx — timestamps from BEFORE the deploy. The model:

1. Read the SOURCE file in `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh`
2. Found `2>&1` and "no JSONL parsing" in source
3. Concluded "this is the bug, the runtime must be doing this"
4. Wrote a detailed root-cause issue (#18473) based on that conclusion
5. Implemented a fix (#18498/t2025) based on the same conclusion

All of which was wrong because the runtime had already been running the FIXED code for ~30 minutes before the investigation began. A single `stat` command at the start would have surfaced "deployed file mtime 02:09, deployed file already has the fix, the symptoms in the log are historical" — and the investigation would have been "verify the deployed fix actually works" instead of "design a fix from scratch".

### Why this is a system-prompt rule, not a workflow doc reference

System-prompt rules are always in context. Workflow doc references require the model to remember to read the doc. For diagnostic discipline that should fire EVERY time a runtime investigation begins — not just when the model happens to think about workflow docs — the rule has to live where it can't be missed. `prompts/build.txt` is the right home because it's the always-present quality discipline layer.

### Why a separate rule from #18508 (Section 0 for implementation)

Both rules are about "check the world before believing your model of it", but they fire at different times and against different artifacts:

| Rule | Triggers when | Checks against | Fixes what |
|------|---------------|----------------|------------|
| #18508 | About to write code | Recent commits, merged PRs, in-flight work | Duplicate work |
| t2036 | About to investigate runtime symptoms | Deployed file mtime vs source commit | Stale-symptom mis-investigation |

A model that has #18508 in context still benefits from t2036 because the temporal-duplicate check fires when you've decided to implement; the deployed-vs-source check fires earlier, when you're still deciding what's broken. Both can be true: I had t2017 in context (which is the review-side equivalent of #18508) and I still failed both checks in #18473, in part because the rule for "investigating" wasn't explicit anywhere.

### Effect

- Catches the specific failure mode that produced #18473 → #18498/t2025 → close-as-duplicate cascade
- Maximum 14-line addition to `build.txt` (the file already has many comparable entries — adding one more doesn't bloat it)
- Costs nothing at runtime: just a one-time `stat` + `git log` per investigation
- Composes with #18508 (different failure modes, additive)

## Tier

### Tier checklist

- [x] **2 or fewer files to modify?** Yes — 1 file (`prompts/build.txt`)
- [ ] **Complete code blocks for every edit?** Yes, but the exact line number for the insertion depends on the current state of `build.txt` and may need adjustment by the implementer
- [x] **No judgment or design decisions?** Borderline — the WORDING matters because it's a system prompt. A small amount of editorial judgement is involved in fitting the new rule alongside existing entries without disrupting the section's voice
- [x] **No error handling or fallback logic to design?** Yes — pure text addition
- [x] **Estimate 1h or less?** Yes — ~15 minutes
- [x] **4 or fewer acceptance criteria?** Yes — 3

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard` (Sonnet) — not `tier:simple` because system-prompt edits warrant the editorial attention that Haiku's strict copy-paste bar doesn't accommodate. The verbatim text above is a starting point; the implementer should integrate it cleanly with the existing section voice and numbering.

**Origin label:** `needs-maintainer-review` (NOT `auto-dispatch`). System-prompt edits affect every future agent session and deserve human review with full awareness of blast radius. A worker dispatched to edit its own system prompt is a recursive footgun pattern worth avoiding by default.

## How (Approach)

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/prompts/build.txt` — add a new numbered entry to the "Error Prevention (top recurring patterns)" section (or whatever section currently houses the numbered diagnostic rules)

### Implementation steps

1. Read `.agents/prompts/build.txt` and locate the "Error Prevention" section (currently houses entries 1-8 covering webfetch failures, markdown formatter, file_not_found, edit:other, glob:other, repo slug hallucination, AI-generated issue quality, prompt injection)
2. Add a new numbered entry (the next free slot — likely `# 9.` but verify) using the verbatim text above as the starting point
3. Adjust the wording to match the section's existing voice (compact, action-oriented, with concrete bash commands where applicable)
4. Verify the cross-reference to "section 7 (Pre-implementation discovery)" makes sense — depends on whether #18508 has landed by the time this is implemented. If not yet, adjust the cross-reference to be forward-looking ("see also issue #18508")
5. Verify line count: the new entry should add ~14-18 lines. If significantly longer, condense.

### Verification

```bash
# 1. The new numbered entry exists
grep -A1 "Stale-symptom investigations" .agents/prompts/build.txt
# Expected: new entry text

# 2. The file still parses cleanly (no broken markdown / no orphaned headers)
markdownlint-cli2 .agents/prompts/build.txt
# Expected: 0 errors

# 3. The total line count increase is modest (< 25 lines added)
git diff --stat origin/main -- .agents/prompts/build.txt
# Expected: ~15-20 line insertion, 0 deletions
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.agents/prompts/build.txt` contains a new numbered entry under the "Error Prevention" section that explicitly addresses the deployed-vs-source mismatch for runtime investigations
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "Stale-symptom|deployed.*source|deployed copy"
    path: ".agents/prompts/build.txt"
  ```
- [ ] The entry includes a concrete `stat` + `git log` command that the model can copy-paste during an investigation (not just a vague "check the deployed version")
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: 'stat -f.*aidevops/agents/scripts'
    path: ".agents/prompts/build.txt"
  ```
- [ ] `markdownlint-cli2 .agents/prompts/build.txt` exits 0 and the section's existing voice is preserved
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "markdownlint-cli2 .agents/prompts/build.txt"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- **Why "Error Prevention" section and not a new section?** Because the failure mode this rule prevents is exactly the kind of recurring-error pattern that section already catalogues (webfetch failures, markdown formatter, file_not_found, etc.). A new section would dilute the structure; a new entry inside the existing section integrates naturally.
- **Why a `stat` command, not a more elaborate diagnostic helper?** Because diagnostic discipline that requires "first install/run a helper" is friction that gets skipped. A single `stat` invocation that any model already knows how to run has the lowest barrier to actual use. If the rule warrants automation later, a helper can be added — but the rule itself should be runnable from memory.
- **Why not check ALL deployed files?** Because the rule is about "investigations rooted in runtime symptoms". When you're investigating a pulse log entry, you already know which file is suspect (the log line tells you). Checking only the relevant file keeps the rule actionable; checking all files is busy-work.
- **Cross-referencing #18508:** The text references "section 7 (Pre-implementation discovery)" because that's where #18508's rule is intended to live. If #18508 ends up in a different section, this cross-reference needs updating at implementation time. Both PRs should not block on each other — the rules are independent and either can land first.
- **Non-goals:**
  - Adding the rule to `workflows/*.md` files (those are read on-demand; this needs to live in the always-loaded prompt)
  - Implementing a "deployed file diff" helper (premature optimization — the rule is the behaviour change, not the tooling)
  - Updating `reference/customization.md` (already documents deployed-vs-source for editing purposes; this rule covers the diagnostic angle which is distinct)
  - Updating `agent-routing.md` or any other doc — system-prompt rules don't need cross-references to be effective

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/prompts/build.txt` — target file (Error Prevention section)
- `.agents/reference/customization.md` — adjacent guidance about deployed vs source for editing (different angle, no change needed)
- `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` — the deployed copy directory the rule references
- `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/` — the source directory the rule contrasts against

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** none (rule is independent — composes with #18508 but doesn't require it)
- **Related:** #18508 (Pre-implementation discovery — sibling failure mode for the implementation phase rather than the investigation phase)
- **External:** none

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Locate insertion site + read context | 3m | Find the right section, match the voice |
| Write the entry | 5m | Adapt verbatim text to fit the section |
| Verification | 2m | markdownlint + diff inspection |
| Commit + PR | 5m | Conventional commit, PR body explaining the failure mode |
| **Total** | **~15m** | |

### Implementation Steps

**Step 1: Re-read the current Job 3 structure.**

```bash
git fetch origin main
sed -n '440,730p' .github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml
```

Note the actual line numbers — t2018 + t2030 + future merges will have shifted them since this brief was written. The structural anchors that should still be present:

- `retrigger-pr-checks:` job header
- `Find linked PRs and re-evaluate gate` step
- `for PR_NUM in $OPEN_PRS; do` outer loop
- `for ISSUE_NUM in $LINKED_ISSUES; do` inner loop (this is what gets DELETED)
- `# Post final status` block
- `# t2018: refresh the REQUIRED CheckRun by re-running Job 1.` block

**Step 2: Identify what to delete.**

Delete the entire inner `for ISSUE_NUM in $LINKED_ISSUES; do ... done` loop AND the surrounding "BLOCKED=false / REASONS=" / "Post final status if BLOCKED" infrastructure that depends on it. That's roughly the block from "Get PR body and labels to find ALL linked issues" down to the closing `done` of the inner loop, plus the conditional post-final-status block that consumes `BLOCKED`.

Keep:

- The for-PR loop header and HEAD_SHA lookup
- The early "post pending status while we evaluate" block (lines ~516-522)
- The t2018 `rerun-failed-jobs` block
- The closing `done` of the outer for-PR loop

**Step 3: Replace the deleted block with a pending-status post.**

After the existing pending status post, insert a NEW post with a clearer message:

```bash
            # t2037: Job 3 no longer evaluates gate state itself. The
            # authoritative evaluation is in Job 1 (check-pr) which we
            # trigger via rerun-failed-jobs below. Post a pending status
            # so the dashboard shows the in-progress refresh; Job 1's
            # final post-status step will overwrite it on completion.
            gh api "repos/${REPO}/statuses/${HEAD_SHA}" \
              --method POST \
              -f state=pending \
              -f context="maintainer-gate" \
              -f description="Refreshing via Job 1 rerun (issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} updated)" \
              2>/dev/null || true
```

**Step 4: Verify the t2018 rerun block's edge cases.**

The t2018 block already handles two cases that matter post-refactor:

- **No prior Job 1 run for this HEAD SHA** (rare — implies the PR was opened during a window when Job 1 hadn't fired) → t2018 logs "No prior maintainer-gate run found" and skips. Job 3's pending status remains visible until the next pull_request event triggers Job 1 fresh. Acceptable degradation.
- **Latest Job 1 run was success** → t2018 short-circuits with "already succeeded — no refresh needed". The pending status Job 3 posted gets superseded by Job 1's existing success. Acceptable.
- **Latest Job 1 run was failure/cancelled** → t2018 calls rerun-failed-jobs. Job 1 reruns, re-reads issue state, posts fresh status. This is the happy path.

No new edge cases introduced by the refactor.

**Step 5: Visual diff check.**

```bash
git diff .github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml | wc -l   # expect ~150-200 deleted lines
git diff .github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml | grep -c "^-"   # most should be deletions
python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml'))"
```

The job count for `maintainer-gate.yml` should still be the same (Job 3 still exists, just smaller). The required CheckRun name `Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` is unchanged (it's Job 1's job name).

**Step 6: Runtime verification on a real PR.**

This refactor must be exercised end-to-end before merging. Suggested test:

1. Create a small dummy PR (e.g., a comment fix in a doc file) with `origin:interactive` and a linked issue that has `needs-maintainer-review` and no assignee.
2. Observe Job 1 fail with the gate.
3. Add the assignee or run `sudo aidevops approve`.
4. Observe Job 3 fire on the issue event.
5. Observe Job 3 post the pending `maintainer-gate` context.
6. Observe Job 3 trigger Job 1 rerun.
7. Observe Job 1 produce the new success CheckRun.
8. Observe the PR become mergeable.

If any step fails, the refactor is broken.

### Verification

```bash
python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml'))" \
  && grep -c "for ISSUE_NUM in \$LINKED_ISSUES" .github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml
# Expect 1 (only Job 1's loop should remain — Job 3's inner loop deleted)
```

# t2037: refactor(maintainer-gate): delete Job 3 inline gate logic, delegate authoritative state to Job 1

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-04-13
- **Session:** OpenCode:interactive (gap-closing pass that shipped t2015/t2018/t2027–t2030/t2034)
- **Created by:** marcusquinn (ai-interactive)
- **Parent task:** none
- **Conversation context:** During the gap-closing session I shipped t2018 (Job 3 reruns Job 1 for required CheckRun refresh) and t2030 (Check -1 moved out of the empty-linked-issues branch). Both were narrow surgical fixes against a deeper structural issue: **Job 3 of `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml` duplicates ~90 lines of Job 1's gate-evaluation logic inline.** When I shipped t2030 (Check -1 expansion) on Job 1, CodeRabbit independently flagged on the t2030 PR review that **Job 3 does not have the parallel `origin:interactive` exemption** — third-party confirmation that the duplication is already drifting in production code, not just theoretical risk. This task ships the underlying refactor: Job 3 stops evaluating gate state itself and becomes pure plumbing that delegates to Job 1 via the t2018 rerun mechanism.

## What

Job 3 (`retrigger-pr-checks`) in `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml` no longer contains the inline `for ISSUE_NUM in $LINKED_ISSUES; do ... Check 1 ... Check 2 ... done` evaluation block. Instead, Job 3:

1. Finds linked PRs referencing the updated issue (current logic, kept).
2. For each PR: posts a `pending` `maintainer-gate` status context with description "Re-evaluating via Job 1 rerun…" so the dashboard reflects in-progress refresh.
3. Calls the t2018 `rerun-failed-jobs` block (current logic, kept) to trigger Job 1 to re-evaluate against current issue state.
4. Lets Job 1's run produce the authoritative `maintainer-gate` status context AND the `Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` CheckRun.

Net effect: **Job 1 is the single source of truth for gate evaluation logic.** Adding/changing a gate rule means editing Job 1 only, not Job 1 + Job 3.

End-state: Job 3 shrinks from ~240 lines to ~80 lines. The inline evaluation (currently `maintainer-gate.yml:596-685` plus the post-final-status block) is deleted. Job 3's surface becomes: trigger conditions → find PRs → post pending status → trigger Job 1 rerun → done.

## Why

**Drift is now confirmed in production, not theoretical.** The session that shipped t2030 (Check -1 out of empty-linked-issues branch on Job 1) **did not** apply the same fix to Job 3, because Job 3 has its own copy of the gate logic and t2030 was scoped to Job 1. CodeRabbit's review on PR #18512 explicitly flagged this:

> Job 3 does not include the `origin:interactive` exemption that Job 1 now has. PRs that hit Job 3's evaluation path will still be blocked on linked-issue checks even when they should pass via the maintainer shortcut.

That's exactly the failure mode Job 1's t2030 fix was supposed to eliminate. The next maintainer-authored interactive PR that triggers Job 3 (e.g., when a label changes after PR creation) will get the OLD behaviour from Job 3 and the NEW behaviour from Job 1 — depending on which produces the visible signal first, the user sees inconsistent gate state.

**Why not just mirror t2030 into Job 3.** Mirroring fixes the immediate inconsistency but leaves the duplication in place. The next gate-rule change will hit the same problem. Eliminating Job 3's inline evaluation entirely solves the class of bug, not just the latest instance. CodeRabbit is unlikely to flag a fourth one if we close it now.

**Why this is a real cost, not just code smell.** Every time Job 1's gate logic changes — new exemption, new check, new edge case — there's an open question of whether to mirror it into Job 3. That question forces a maintainer code review every time. With the refactor, Job 1 is authoritative and the question disappears.

## Tier

### Tier checklist

- [x] **≤2 files to modify?** — 1 file: `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml`
- [ ] **Complete code blocks for every edit?** — partial. The new Job 3 structure is described below in pseudocode, but the exact YAML formatting requires reading and adapting current line numbers at execution time (the file has changed since this brief was written).
- [ ] **No judgment or design decisions?** — moderate. Two judgment calls: (a) what does Job 3 post on the `maintainer-gate` status context while waiting for Job 1's rerun, (b) what to do if Job 1 has never run for the PR's HEAD SHA (degenerate edge case).
- [x] **No error handling or fallback logic to design?** — error paths reuse the t2018 fallback (warning + continue).

## Context & Decisions

**Why delete Job 3's inline evaluation entirely instead of mirroring t2030 into it.** Mirroring fixes the immediate Check -1 inconsistency but leaves the duplication structure in place. **Why not also delete Job 3's `find linked PRs` logic.** Job 3 still needs to know which PRs to refresh. The find-PRs path is data discovery, not gate evaluation. It stays.

**Why this can't be tier:simple.** Writing a bash deletion is mechanical, but verifying that NO gate-relevant signal is lost requires reading the current Job 3 carefully, identifying every consumer of the deleted code, and checking the t2018 rerun edge cases.
