title: t2063: fix: inline brief into issue body so workers receive full context on first dispatch
body:
**Task ID:** `t2063` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-04-14
**Tags:** `bug` `auto-dispatch` `interactive`

## Description

fix: inline brief into issue body so workers receive full context on first dispatch — root cause of Sonnet workers failing to solve issues on first pass. Two recent examples (GH#18745 t2059, GH#18746 t2060) had 476-char pointer bodies despite 10-12 KB brief files. Caused by ordering: claim-task-id.sh creates the issue before TODO.md has the ref, so delegation to issue-sync push fails and the bare fallback uses --description verbatim. Then _enrich_update_issue preserves the stub because it lacks the "Synced from TODO.md" sentinel. Fix: (A) claim-task-id _compose_issue_body inlines brief when one exists, appends sentinel; (B) _enrich_update_issue uses brief-file presence as authoritative signal instead of sentinel; (C) dispatch-time guard force-enriches if brief exists but body lacks Task Brief marker; plus case-insensitive heading matcher and template heading-lock.

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh:792-836` (`_compose_issue_body`) — always inline brief when one exists, append sentinel footer.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh:760-787` (`_enrich_update_issue`) — three-case classifier driven by brief-file presence.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh:971-1005` (`_compose_issue_worker_guidance`) — case-insensitive heading match.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` or `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh` — pre-dispatch brief-body guard. Place it in the same Layer 6 path where other dispatch guards live.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/templates/brief-template.md` — lock the How-section and subsection headings with a `<!-- HEADING LOCK -->` comment and normative language.
- **NEW:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-brief-inline-classifier.sh` — unit test covering:
  - `claim-task-id.sh` path A: terse description + brief exists → body contains `## Task Brief`
  - `claim-task-id.sh` path B: terse description + no brief → body is terse (no regression)
  - `_enrich_update_issue` case 1: brief exists → `do_body_update=true`
  - `_enrich_update_issue` case 2: no brief, no sentinel → `do_body_update=false` (preserve)
  - `_enrich_update_issue` case 3: no brief, sentinel present → `do_body_update=(current != composed)` (refresh on diff)
  - case-insensitive heading match: `### files to modify` lowercase activates Worker Guidance extraction

### Reference patterns

- **`.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh:1011-1033`** (`_compose_issue_brief`) — canonical brief-append pattern. Reuse by sourcing `issue-sync-lib.sh` from `claim-task-id.sh`, not by duplicating.
- **`.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh:971-1005`** (`_compose_issue_worker_guidance`) — canonical How-section extractor. The `awk '/^## How/ {capture=1; next} /^## / && capture {exit} capture'` pattern is correct; only the downstream subsection matcher needs the case-insensitive fix.
- **`.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh:910`** — the sentinel footer string `*Synced from TODO.md by issue-sync-helper.sh*`. Use `_compose_issue_html_notes_and_footer` as the single source of the footer format.
- **`.agents/scripts/tests/test-privacy-guard.sh`** — stub style for new test file.

### Implementation Steps

**Step 1 — Source issue-sync-lib.sh from claim-task-id.sh.** At the top of `claim-task-id.sh`, alongside the existing helper imports, source `issue-sync-lib.sh` so `_compose_issue_worker_guidance`, `_compose_issue_brief`, and `_compose_issue_html_notes_and_footer` become available. Guard with `[[ -z "${ISSUE_SYNC_LIB_SOURCED:-}" ]]` to avoid double-sourcing.

**Step 2 — Rewrite `_compose_issue_body` in claim-task-id.sh** (lines 792-836). New logic:

```bash
_compose_issue_body() {
    local title="$1"
    local description="$2"

    # Extract task ID from title
    local task_id=""
    [[ "$title" =~ ^(t[0-9]+) ]] && task_id="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"

    local brief_file=""
    if [[ -n "$task_id" ]]; then
        brief_file="${REPO_PATH}/todo/tasks/${task_id}-brief.md"
    fi

    local body=""

    # Summary paragraph: caller's --description, OR brief's What section, OR nothing
    if [[ -n "$description" ]]; then
        body="$description"
    elif [[ -f "$brief_file" ]]; then
        local brief_what
        brief_what=$(_read_brief_what_section "$task_id" "$REPO_PATH") || true
        [[ -n "$brief_what" ]] && body="## Task"$'\n\n'"$brief_what"
    fi

    # If brief exists, inline Worker Guidance + full Task Brief
    if [[ -f "$brief_file" ]]; then
        body=$(_compose_issue_worker_guidance "$body" "$brief_file")
        body=$(_compose_issue_brief "$body" "$brief_file")
        # Append sentinel + signature footer via the shared composer
        body=$(_compose_issue_html_notes_and_footer "$body" "")
    else
        # No brief: existing behavior — refuse to create stub, or use description as-is
        if [[ -z "$body" ]]; then
            log_error "No --description provided and no brief file found at todo/tasks/${task_id}-brief.md"
            log_error "Issue creation skipped — create the brief first, or provide --description"
            echo ""
            return 1
        fi
        # Append signature footer via gh-signature-helper
        local sig_helper="${SCRIPT_DIR}/gh-signature-helper.sh"
        if [[ -x "$sig_helper" ]]; then
            local sig_footer
            sig_footer=$("$sig_helper" footer --body "$body" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
            [[ -n "$sig_footer" ]] && body="$body"$'\n'"$sig_footer"
        fi
    fi

    echo "$body"
    return 0
}
```

**Step 3 — Rewrite `_enrich_update_issue` in issue-sync-helper.sh** (lines 760-787). New logic:

```bash
_enrich_update_issue() {
    local repo="$1" num="$2" task_id="$3" title="$4" body="$5"
    local do_body_update=true

    if [[ "$FORCE_ENRICH" != "true" ]]; then
        # Source of truth: does a brief file exist on disk?
        local project_root brief_file
        project_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)
        brief_file="${project_root}/todo/tasks/${task_id}-brief.md"

        local current_body
        current_body=$(gh issue view "$num" --repo "$repo" --json body -q .body 2>/dev/null || echo "")

        if [[ -f "$brief_file" ]]; then
            # Brief exists → brief is authoritative, refresh if different
            if [[ "$current_body" == "$body" ]]; then
                print_info "Body unchanged on #$num ($task_id), skipping API call"
                do_body_update=false
            fi
            # else: refresh
        elif [[ "$current_body" == *"Synced from TODO.md by issue-sync-helper.sh"* ]]; then
            # No brief, has sentinel: previously synced → refresh on diff (existing)
            if [[ "$current_body" == "$body" ]]; then
                print_info "Body unchanged on #$num ($task_id), skipping API call"
                do_body_update=false
            fi
        else
            # No brief, no sentinel: genuine external content → preserve (existing)
            print_info "Preserving external body on #$num ($task_id) — no brief file, no sentinel (use --force to override)"
            do_body_update=false
        fi
    fi

    if [[ "$do_body_update" == "true" ]]; then
        if gh issue edit "$num" --repo "$repo" --title "$title" --body "$body" 2>/dev/null; then
            return 0
        fi
        print_error "Failed to enrich body on #$num ($task_id)"
        return 1
    fi
    # Still update title even when body is preserved/skipped (GH#18411)
    if gh issue edit "$num" --repo "$repo" --title "$title" 2>/dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi
    print_error "Failed to enrich title on #$num ($task_id)"
    return 1
}
```

**Step 4 — Case-insensitive heading match in `_compose_issue_worker_guidance`** (issue-sync-lib.sh:971-1005). Change:

```bash
has_files=$(echo "$how_section" | grep -c '### Files to Modify\|EDIT:\|NEW:' || true)
has_steps=$(echo "$how_section" | grep -c '### Implementation Steps' || true)
has_verify=$(echo "$how_section" | grep -c '### Verification' || true)
```

to:

```bash
has_files=$(echo "$how_section" | grep -ic '### Files to Modify\|EDIT:\|NEW:' || true)
has_steps=$(echo "$how_section" | grep -ic '### Implementation Steps' || true)
has_verify=$(echo "$how_section" | grep -ic '### Verification' || true)
```

`-i` flag makes grep case-insensitive. Also remove the dead `has_verify` assignment if it remains unused, or add it to the condition.

**Step 5 — Pre-dispatch brief-body guard.** Add a small check function somewhere in the dispatch path (recommend adding to `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` as a sibling of `is_assigned`, or as a new phase in `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` before worker spawn):

```bash
# _ensure_body_has_brief: if a brief exists on disk for the task but the issue
# body lacks the ## Task Brief marker, force-enrich before dispatch.
_ensure_body_has_brief() {
    local issue_num="$1" repo="$2"

    # Resolve task_id from issue title
    local task_id
    task_id=$(gh issue view "$issue_num" --repo "$repo" --json title -q .title 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '^t[0-9]+' | head -1)
    [[ -z "$task_id" ]] && return 0  # No task_id → nothing to check

    # Check for brief file (via gh API on the canonical repo, not local worktree)
    local brief_exists
    brief_exists=$(gh api "repos/${repo}/contents/todo/tasks/${task_id}-brief.md" --jq .name 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    [[ -z "$brief_exists" ]] && return 0  # No brief → nothing to enforce

    # Check if body already has the Task Brief marker
    local body
    body=$(gh issue view "$issue_num" --repo "$repo" --json body -q .body 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if echo "$body" | grep -q "## Task Brief\|## Worker Guidance"; then
        return 0  # Already upgraded
    fi

    # Force-enrich via issue-sync-helper.sh
    print_warning "Issue #$issue_num has brief on disk but stub body — force-enriching before dispatch"
    FORCE_ENRICH=true "${SCRIPT_DIR}/issue-sync-helper.sh" enrich --task-id "$task_id" 2>&1 | tail -5 || true
    return 0
}
```

Wire it into the dispatch path immediately before the worker spawn (after dedup checks pass, before `headless-runtime-helper.sh run`).

**Step 6 — Template heading-lock.** In `templates/brief-template.md`, above the `## How` section, add:

```markdown
<!-- HEADING LOCK (t2063): the following heading must remain exactly "## How"
     (optionally with " (Approach)" suffix). The subsection headings must be
     exactly "### Files to Modify", "### Implementation Steps", and
     "### Verification". issue-sync-lib.sh:_compose_issue_worker_guidance
     extracts these sections for the Worker Guidance block in the issue body.
     Case-insensitive match is applied, but stick to the canonical casing. -->
```

**Step 7 — Unit tests.** Create `tests/test-brief-inline-classifier.sh` with the six cases listed in "Files to Modify". Use the same stub-project pattern as `tests/test-privacy-guard.sh`: create a temp dir with a fake repo structure, drop a brief file or don't, call the function under test, assert the output.

**Step 8 — Full test suite + shellcheck.**

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-brief-inline-classifier.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync.sh  # if it exists; else skip
shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh
```

### Verification

```bash
# Unit tests pass
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-brief-inline-classifier.sh

# ShellCheck clean on all touched files
shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh \
           .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh \
           .agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh \
           .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh

# Integration: new issue created via claim-task-id with existing brief
# has rich body
cd /tmp && mkdir -p test-t2063 && cd test-t2063
git init >/dev/null 2>&1
mkdir -p todo/tasks
cat > todo/tasks/t9999-brief.md <<'EOF'
# t9999: test brief

## Task Brief

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->

# t2063: fix brief-to-issue-body inlining so workers receive full context on first dispatch

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-04-14
- **Session:** claude-code:interactive (claude-opus-4-6)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** User observed Sonnet workers failing to solve issues on first pass. Root-cause investigation found two recent examples (GH#18745 t2059, GH#18746 t2060) where issue bodies were 476-char pointers ("See todo/tasks/tNNN-brief.md for details") despite 10-12 KB brief files existing on disk. Traced to an ordering bug in `claim-task-id.sh` + a preservation gate in `issue-sync-helper.sh` that together produce and then protect stub bodies. Full RCA in this session's transcript.

## What

Make the brief file on disk the authoritative source of truth for issue body content. Three coordinated code changes plus a heading-lock in the template:

1. **Claim-task-id bare path** (`claim-task-id.sh:_compose_issue_body`): when a brief file exists at `todo/tasks/${task_id}-brief.md`, always inline Worker Guidance + full Task Brief into the issue body on creation — regardless of whether `--description` was provided. The `--description` becomes the summary paragraph at the top; the brief content follows. Append the same `*Synced from TODO.md by issue-sync-helper.sh*` sentinel footer that the rich path writes, so subsequent enrich calls are allowed to refresh the body.

2. **Enrich gate** (`issue-sync-helper.sh:_enrich_update_issue`): replace the binary sentinel check with a three-case classifier driven by brief-file presence, not body length. If a brief file exists on disk, the brief is authoritative and the body gets refreshed. If no brief exists, the existing sentinel-based preserve/refresh logic stays. Zero character thresholds.

3. **Dispatch-time guard** (`dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:_has_active_claim` path, or the pulse dispatch wrapper): before dispatching a worker, if the issue has a corresponding brief file on disk AND the current issue body lacks the `## Task Brief` marker, force-enrich the body first. This is defense-in-depth — it should never fire once (1) and (2) ship, but it catches any future bypass.

4. **Heading-lock** (`templates/brief-template.md`) + **case-insensitive matcher** (`issue-sync-lib.sh:_compose_issue_worker_guidance`): lock the How-section heading to `## How` (optionally with ` (Approach)` suffix) and lock the subsection headings to `### Files to Modify`, `### Implementation Steps`, `### Verification`. Make the matcher case-insensitive so a lowercase `### files to modify` still activates the Worker Guidance extraction. An adjacent fragility caught during the same investigation.

## Why

Observable failure modes the fix resolves:

- **GH#18746 (t2060)**: issue body is "Flip complete_task() to extract... See todo/tasks/t2060-brief.md for details." — 476 chars. Brief file is 11,205 bytes. Two workers raced the issue producing PR #18760 (open, unmerged) and PR #18769 (merged). Duplicate work, manual cleanup.
- **GH#18745 (t2059)**: identical shape. 476-char pointer body, 10,155-byte brief file. Still in-review.

Causal chain:

1. Interactive `/new-task` or `/define` calls `claim-task-id.sh --title "..." --description "<terse>"`.
2. `claim-task-id.sh:create_github_issue` tries `_try_issue_sync_delegation` first. Delegation calls `issue-sync-helper.sh push $task_id`, which requires the TODO entry to already be in TODO.md. The TODO entry is written AFTER the claim call. Delegation fails silently.
3. Fallback `_compose_issue_body` (claim-task-id.sh:792) uses the `--description` arg verbatim. Issue is created with the 476-char stub body.
4. Caller writes the brief file + TODO entry + pushes (observed: 20 minutes later on t2060).
5. CI `issue-sync.yml` runs on the TODO push → `_enrich_process_task` composes a rich body via `compose_issue_body` (which inlines Worker Guidance + Task Brief) → calls `_enrich_update_issue`.
6. `_enrich_update_issue` at `issue-sync-helper.sh:766` sees the existing body lacks the `"Synced from TODO.md by issue-sync-helper.sh"` sentinel footer → classifies it as "external human content" → `do_body_update=false` → preserves the terse stub and only updates labels/title.
7. Worker dispatched against the stub body. Must burn tokens (observed ~1500-3000 per attempt on Sonnet) discovering the brief path, reading it, re-orienting. Dedup window closes during exploration → second worker dispatched. Two PRs race. Duplicate delivery, noisy audit trail.

Root architectural problem: the brief file and the issue body are **two copies of the same content**, and the enrich gate was built to protect one copy from the other. With the fix, the brief file is the single source of truth and the body is a view — no preservation needed, no drift, no race.

Secondary benefit: briefs edited after issue creation (refining a How section a day later) currently never reach the worker. Under the fix, any subsequent enrich pass refreshes the body from the current brief. No drift.

## Tier

### Tier checklist

- [x] **More than 2 files to modify?** Yes (claim-task-id.sh, issue-sync-helper.sh, issue-sync-lib.sh, dispatch-dedup-helper.sh, templates/brief-template.md, tests) — disqualifies `tier:simple`.
- [ ] Skeleton code blocks? No — every change is explicit with verbatim patterns cited below.
- [ ] Error/fallback logic to design? No — brief-exists-on-disk is a boolean; sentinel logic stays unchanged for the no-brief case.
- [x] Estimate > 1h? Yes (~3-4h) — disqualifies `tier:simple`.
- [ ] More than 4 acceptance criteria? 6 criteria, each mechanically checkable.
- [ ] Judgment keywords? No — the rule is "brief exists → brief wins; no brief → preserve".

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Mechanical implementation following established patterns in the codebase. The new composition logic reuses the existing `_compose_issue_worker_guidance` and `_compose_issue_brief` helpers. The enrich classifier is a 5-line change. No architectural decisions, no novel design.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh:792-836` (`_compose_issue_body`) — always inline brief when one exists, append sentinel footer.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh:760-787` (`_enrich_update_issue`) — three-case classifier driven by brief-file presence.

```bash
_compose_issue_body() {
    local title="$1"
    local description="$2"

    # Extract task ID from title
    local task_id=""
    [[ "$title" =~ ^(t[0-9]+) ]] && task_id="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"

    local brief_file=""
    if [[ -n "$task_id" ]]; then
        brief_file="${REPO_PATH}/todo/tasks/${task_id}-brief.md"
    fi

    local body=""

    # Summary paragraph: caller's --description, OR brief's What section, OR nothing
    if [[ -n "$description" ]]; then
        body="$description"
    elif [[ -f "$brief_file" ]]; then
        local brief_what
        brief_what=$(_read_brief_what_section "$task_id" "$REPO_PATH") || true
        [[ -n "$brief_what" ]] && body="## Task"$'\n\n'"$brief_what"
    fi

    # If brief exists, inline Worker Guidance + full Task Brief
    if [[ -f "$brief_file" ]]; then
        body=$(_compose_issue_worker_guidance "$body" "$brief_file")
        body=$(_compose_issue_brief "$body" "$brief_file")
        # Append sentinel + signature footer via the shared composer
        body=$(_compose_issue_html_notes_and_footer "$body" "")
    else
        # No brief: existing behavior — refuse to create stub, or use description as-is
        if [[ -z "$body" ]]; then
            log_error "No --description provided and no brief file found at todo/tasks/${task_id}-brief.md"
            log_error "Issue creation skipped — create the brief first, or provide --description"
            echo ""
            return 1
        fi
        # Append signature footer via gh-signature-helper
        local sig_helper="${SCRIPT_DIR}/gh-signature-helper.sh"
        if [[ -x "$sig_helper" ]]; then
            local sig_footer
            sig_footer=$("$sig_helper" footer --body "$body" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
            [[ -n "$sig_footer" ]] && body="$body"$'\n'"$sig_footer"
        fi
    fi

    echo "$body"
    return 0
}
```

**Step 3 — Rewrite `_enrich_update_issue` in issue-sync-helper.sh** (lines 760-787). New logic:

```bash
_enrich_update_issue() {
    local repo="$1" num="$2" task_id="$3" title="$4" body="$5"
    local do_body_update=true

    if [[ "$FORCE_ENRICH" != "true" ]]; then
        # Source of truth: does a brief file exist on disk?
        local project_root brief_file
        project_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)
        brief_file="${project_root}/todo/tasks/${task_id}-brief.md"

        local current_body
        current_body=$(gh issue view "$num" --repo "$repo" --json body -q .body 2>/dev/null || echo "")

        if [[ -f "$brief_file" ]]; then
            # Brief exists → brief is authoritative, refresh if different
            if [[ "$current_body" == "$body" ]]; then
                print_info "Body unchanged on #$num ($task_id), skipping API call"
                do_body_update=false
            fi
            # else: refresh
        elif [[ "$current_body" == *"Synced from TODO.md by issue-sync-helper.sh"* ]]; then
            # No brief, has sentinel: previously synced → refresh on diff (existing)
            if [[ "$current_body" == "$body" ]]; then
                print_info "Body unchanged on #$num ($task_id), skipping API call"
                do_body_update=false
            fi
        else
            # No brief, no sentinel: genuine external content → preserve (existing)
            print_info "Preserving external body on #$num ($task_id) — no brief file, no sentinel (use --force to override)"
            do_body_update=false
        fi
    fi

    if [[ "$do_body_update" == "true" ]]; then
        if gh issue edit "$num" --repo "$repo" --title "$title" --body "$body" 2>/dev/null; then
            return 0
        fi
        print_error "Failed to enrich body on #$num ($task_id)"
        return 1
    fi
    # Still update title even when body is preserved/skipped (GH#18411)
    if gh issue edit "$num" --repo "$repo" --title "$title" 2>/dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi
    print_error "Failed to enrich title on #$num ($task_id)"
    return 1
}
```

```

`-i` flag makes grep case-insensitive. Also remove the dead `has_verify` assignment if it remains unused, or add it to the condition.

**Step 5 — Pre-dispatch brief-body guard.** Add a small check function somewhere in the dispatch path (recommend adding to `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` as a sibling of `is_assigned`, or as a new phase in `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` before worker spawn):

```bash
# _ensure_body_has_brief: if a brief exists on disk for the task but the issue
# body lacks the ## Task Brief marker, force-enrich before dispatch.
_ensure_body_has_brief() {
    local issue_num="$1" repo="$2"

    # Resolve task_id from issue title
    local task_id
    task_id=$(gh issue view "$issue_num" --repo "$repo" --json title -q .title 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '^t[0-9]+' | head -1)
    [[ -z "$task_id" ]] && return 0  # No task_id → nothing to check

    # Check for brief file (via gh API on the canonical repo, not local worktree)
    local brief_exists
    brief_exists=$(gh api "repos/${repo}/contents/todo/tasks/${task_id}-brief.md" --jq .name 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    [[ -z "$brief_exists" ]] && return 0  # No brief → nothing to enforce

    # Check if body already has the Task Brief marker
    local body
    body=$(gh issue view "$issue_num" --repo "$repo" --json body -q .body 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if echo "$body" | grep -q "## Task Brief\|## Worker Guidance"; then
        return 0  # Already upgraded
    fi

    # Force-enrich via issue-sync-helper.sh
    print_warning "Issue #$issue_num has brief on disk but stub body — force-enriching before dispatch"
    FORCE_ENRICH=true "${SCRIPT_DIR}/issue-sync-helper.sh" enrich --task-id "$task_id" 2>&1 | tail -5 || true
    return 0
}
```

## What

Nothing in the ratchet ever required a *new* file to be smell-free before landing. Subsystems arrive as 300-line mega-modules and nobody refactors because "it worked when it landed".

## What

Add a CI check that runs `qlty smells --all --sarif` *against just the files newly added in the PR* (via `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A origin/main...HEAD`). If any newly-added source file (`.py`, `.mjs`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.sh`, `.rb`, etc. — delegate the filter to qlty's own language detection) reports **any** smell, fail the check unless the PR carries a documented justification label.

This is narrowly scoped: it only checks files that are brand-new in the PR. Existing files are not re-checked (that's covered by t2065's regression gate). The point is to prevent debt accumulation from new subsystems.

## Why

- **Historical pattern:** every top-5 smell file in the current snapshot was a new file at some point. The higgsfield video subsystem landed in a single PR adding `higgsfield-video.mjs` (1500+ lines, cyclomatic chaos). The opencode plugin cluster landed similarly. None had a simplification step before they landed — they shipped complex and stayed complex.
- **Early-stage refactor is free.** A function with cyclomatic 25 at PR time is easy to split — the author still has the context in their head. Three months later, nobody remembers why it's shaped that way and everyone leaves it alone.
- **The existing file-size gate is insufficient.** It only checks shell, it counts lines not complexity, and it only fires at 1500+ lines. A 400-line Python file with cyclomatic 40 sails through.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** Requires CI design, awareness of qlty language detection, override-label handling, and careful scoping (don't break PRs that add fixtures, vendored code, generated files, or templates). Opus-tier design work.

- `NEW: .github/workflows/qlty-new-file-gate.yml` — or as an additional job in `qlty-regression.yml` (from t2065) if cleaner

2. **Detect new files.** `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A origin/main...HEAD` returns added paths. Filter out:

   - Explicit new-file exclusions for docs: `*.md`, `todo/**`, `.github/**` non-workflow
   - Fixture paths matching `**/fixtures/**`, `**/testdata/**` (already in qlty's exclude set)

3. **Run qlty against the filtered list.** `~/.qlty/bin/qlty smells --all --sarif --no-snippets --quiet <file1> <file2> ...` — qlty accepts path arguments. Parse the result, count smells per file.

4. **Fail if any new file has any smell.** Per-file breakdown in the PR comment:

   ```
   New file(s) shipped with qlty smells:
   - `path/to/new-file.py`: 4 smells
     - qlty:function-complexity (cyclomatic 28): parse_envelope at line 45
     - qlty:file-complexity: total 87
     - qlty:return-statements: process_row at line 112 (6 returns)
     - qlty:nested-control-flow: parse_envelope at line 67 (depth 5)
   ```

5. **Override label `new-file-smell-ok`.** Requires the PR description to contain a `## New File Smell Justification` section. The workflow greps for the section; failing that, fails the check even with the label.

```bash
# Workflow lints

# Helper has new subcommand
.agents/scripts/qlty-regression-helper.sh new-files --base HEAD~5 --head HEAD --dry-run

# Smoke test: throwaway PR adding a deliberately smelly new file fails the check

- [ ] New workflow (or added job) runs on PR events and scans only newly-added files
- [ ] Helper supports `new-files` subcommand that returns per-file smell breakdown
- [ ] PRs adding files with qlty smells fail the check unless `new-file-smell-ok` label + justification section present
- [ ] PRs touching only existing files (no new files) skip this check and pass
- [ ] PRs adding doc/fixture/template files (matching qlty exclude patterns) skip this check

- **Why an override label at all?** Because some legitimate new files ship complex: generated code, vendored third-party, fixtures that mirror real-world shapes. The override exists for those, with justification required in the PR body so maintainers can push back on abuse.
- **Why only new files, not modified files?** Modified files are covered by the t2065 regression gate (delta-based). This gate fills the specific "brand-new subsystem lands already smelly" gap.

## Why

- **Two labels for the same thing is a silent footgun.** Workers reading a task that's labelled `tier:reasoning` can't distinguish it from one labelled `tier:thinking`, and the cascade / routing logic has to special-case both. - **The C→A quality campaign will file 10 tasks with `tier:thinking`** (t2064–t2072). Having two labels means these tasks will be visually inconsistent with the 92 existing `tier:reasoning` references. Unifying now avoids the inconsistency.

gh label list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --search "tier:"
#    tier:thinking    Route to opus-tier model for dispatch
#    tier:reasoning   Route to opus-tier model for dispatch
#    tier:standard    Auto-created from TODO.md tag
#    tier:simple      Auto-created from TODO.md tag
```

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: all files in the inventory above (15+ files, 92 occurrences)`
- `EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md` — the `tier:reasoning` description in the "Briefs, Tiers, and Dispatchability" section
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/task-taxonomy.md` — update tier definitions, cascade diagram
- `EDIT: .agents/templates/brief-template.md` — tier checklist wording
- `EDIT: .agents/workflows/brief/tier-reasoning.md` — rename file to `tier-thinking.md`, update all references to the filename
- **GitHub label changes** (executed as part of the PR validation step):
  - Add alias: migrate all open issues from `tier:reasoning` to `tier:thinking` before deletion
  - Delete `tier:reasoning` label
- `EDIT: any helpers that create the label on setup` (search: `gh label create.*tier:reasoning`)

### Implementation Steps

1. **Inventory.** `rg -l "tier:reasoning" .agents/ > /tmp/reasoning-files.txt`. Review each file to distinguish:
   - Simple string references (safe `sed`)
   - Test assertions that hard-code `tier:reasoning` as the expected value (need careful handling)
   - Historical changelog/memory entries (**leave alone** — those are accurate records of past state)

2. **Define migration rules.**
   - **DO** rename: active code (`pulse-*.sh`, `worker-lifecycle-common.sh`), active tests (`test-*.sh`), templates, docs in `reference/` and `workflows/`, AGENTS.md.
   - **DO NOT** rename: `complexity-thresholds-history.md`, `*CHANGELOG*`, git commit messages, memory-helper entries, archived briefs in `todo/tasks/` that were completed under the old name. These are historical artifacts.

3. **Rename.** `sed -i '' 's/tier:reasoning/tier:thinking/g'` on the active-code set. Manually inspect each test file — tests that dedup tier labels may need both names until migration completes.

4. **Handle the `tier:reasoning` GitHub label:**
   - **Step 4a (before PR merge, may be a pre-merge script step):** list all issues with `tier:reasoning` label: `gh issue list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --label "tier:reasoning" --state all --limit 1000`
   - **Step 4b:** for each, add `tier:thinking` and remove `tier:reasoning`:

     ```bash
     gh issue list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --label "tier:reasoning" --state open --json number --jq '.[].number' \
       | while read n; do
           gh issue edit "$n" --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --add-label "tier:thinking" --remove-label "tier:reasoning"
         done
     ```

   - **Step 4c:** closed issues — migrate the label too, so historical label searches remain consistent. Use `--state all` above.
   - **Step 4d:** delete the label: `gh label delete "tier:reasoning" --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --yes`

5. **Update `worker-lifecycle-common.sh` and `pulse-model-routing.sh`** — these are the dispatch routing code paths. A bug here silently breaks dispatch. Model on the existing `tier:thinking` code paths (they already exist — the routing already handles both names, we're just dropping one).

6. **Update tests.**
   - `test-tier-label-dedup.sh` (12 matches) — this test specifically covers the dedup case; rewrite to assert the dedup now has only one label (`tier:thinking`).
   - `test-label-invariants.sh`, `test-cost-circuit-breaker.sh`, `test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh`, `test-issue-sync-tier-extraction.sh` — rename the expected label.

7. **Rename the `tier-reasoning.md` workflow file** to `tier-thinking.md`. Any references to the filename in other docs also get updated.

8. **Update the changelog entry in the PR description** documenting: files changed, GH labels migrated, any issues needing manual review.

### Verification

```bash
# Zero tier:reasoning in active code
rg -l "tier:reasoning" .agents/ | grep -v -E '(CHANGELOG|history|todo/tasks/|memory)' | wc -l
# Expected: 0

# Label dedup
gh label list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --search "tier:" | awk '{print $1}' | sort
# Expected: tier:simple, tier:standard, tier:thinking (no tier:reasoning)

# Tests pass
.agents/scripts/tests/test-tier-label-dedup.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-label-invariants.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-cost-circuit-breaker.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-tier-extraction.sh

# Dispatch dry-run still routes opus
# (manual check — run pulse with a tier:thinking-labelled issue in dry-run mode)
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rg "tier:reasoning" .agents/` returns zero hits in active code (historical files allowed)
  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "test 0 -eq \"$(rg -l 'tier:reasoning' .agents/ 2>/dev/null | grep -v -E '(CHANGELOG|history|todo/tasks/)' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')\""
  ```
- [ ] `gh label list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops` shows no `tier:reasoning` label
- [ ] All previously `tier:reasoning`-labelled issues (open and closed) now carry `tier:thinking` instead
- [ ] `test-tier-label-dedup.sh` passes
- [ ] `test-label-invariants.sh` passes
- [ ] `pulse-model-routing.sh` routes `tier:thinking` to opus (manual smoke check in PR description)
- [ ] Workflow file `tier-reasoning.md` renamed to `tier-thinking.md` with content updated
- [ ] AGENTS.md and task-taxonomy.md updated to describe only `tier:thinking`

## Context & Decisions

- **Why not keep both as aliases?** Aliases compound maintenance cost forever. The rename is cheap now (one PR) and expensive later (every new PR that could reference either name).
- **Why not just delete the label without the rename?** Because 92 references in active code check for `tier:reasoning`; deleting the label would silently break all of them. Rename first, delete last.
- **Historical files are left alone** because they record accurate past state. Rewriting history is a footgun — `git blame` and `grep` for audit trails expect the old string to appear in files that were committed with it.
- **`tier:thinking` wins on naming consistency** with `tier:simple` / `tier:standard` (adjectives describing the cognitive work) and pairs better with user-facing language ("this task needs thinking" vs "this task needs reasoning").

## Relevant Files

Full list from `rg "tier:reasoning" .agents/ -c`:

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tier-label-dedup.sh` (12)
- `.agents/reference/task-taxonomy.md` (12)
- `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh` (7)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh` (6)
- `.agents/templates/brief-template.md` (5)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-label-invariants.sh` (4)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cost-circuit-breaker.sh` (4)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification.sh` (3)
- `.agents/workflows/triage-review.md` (2)
- `.agents/workflows/brief.md` (2)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh` (2)

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` (2)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-model-routing.sh` (2)
- `.agents/workflows/review-issue-pr.md` (1)
- … and the rest of the ~92 matches

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none — can ship standalone
- **Blocks:** t2066 (the sweep rewire assumes `tier:thinking` is canonical) — can be completed in parallel, but t2073 should land first
- **External:** `gh` auth with label-delete permission (already standard for repo owner)

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Research/read | 45m | Full inventory + distinguishing active vs historical |
| Implementation | 2.5h | Rename sweep + test updates + workflow file rename |
| GH label migration | 30m | Script the open+closed issue relabelling |
| Testing | 1h | Run all tier-related tests, dispatch smoke |
| **Total** | **~4.5h** | |

title: t2074: fix(aidevops.sh): guard getent call + add cross-platform command portability rules
body:
## What

`sudo aidevops approve issue <N>` fails on macOS with:

```
/usr/local/bin/aidevops: line 26: getent: command not found
```

## Why

PR #18686 (resolves #18646) added `SUDO_USER` → `getent passwd` home resolution to both `aidevops.sh` and `approval-helper.sh`, but only `approval-helper.sh` got the `command -v getent &>/dev/null` guard (line 33). `aidevops.sh:26` calls `getent` unconditionally when `SUDO_USER` is set and we are root, which is always true under `sudo` on both platforms. On macOS, `getent` does not exist, so the command substitution fails and `set -euo pipefail` kills the script before any subcommand runs.

The commit message for #18686 claimed `macOS unaffected: sudo does not reset HOME; getent not available (fallback to $HOME)` — but this is only true for `approval-helper.sh`, not for `aidevops.sh`.

Also, this is a specific instance of a broader gap: our `bash-compat.md` rules cover bash-version differences (3.2 vs 4+) but not **command-level portability** between macOS (BSD coreutils, no `getent`, has `dscl`) and Linux (GNU coreutils, has `getent`, no `dscl`). A parallel set of rules for command portability would prevent future regressions in both directions.

## How

### Fix A: aidevops.sh one-line guard

Mirror `approval-helper.sh:33` exactly:

```bash
if [[ -n "${SUDO_USER:-}" && "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]] && command -v getent &>/dev/null; then
```

On macOS, `sudo` preserves `$HOME` by default (verified: `env_keep+="HOME MAIL"` in `/etc/sudoers`), so the fallback to `$HOME` is correct.

### Fix B: expand `bash-compat.md` → add cross-platform command portability section

Add a table covering GNU ↔ BSD ↔ macOS command divergences and reference canonical portable patterns (`setup-modules/shell-env.sh:33-38` has the dscl/getent fallback; `aidevops.sh` has `sed_inplace` and `_timeout_cmd`). The existing bash-compat.md is titled "Bash 3.2 Compatibility" — I will rename the H1 to reflect both dimensions.

### Fix C: regression test

Add `.agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-sh-portability.sh` that greps `aidevops.sh` for unguarded `getent`/`dscl`/`gawk`/`gsed` calls and fails if any are found without a `command -v` guard or platform check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `aidevops.sh:26` uses `command -v getent` guard (mirrors `approval-helper.sh:33`)
- [ ] `sudo aidevops approve issue <N>` runs without `getent: command not found` on macOS
- [ ] `bash-compat.md` has a new section "Cross-platform command portability" with GNU ↔ BSD ↔ macOS table
- [ ] `tests/test-aidevops-sh-portability.sh` passes and catches the regression if reintroduced

## Context

- Originating broken commit: 401438c9c (PR #18686, resolves #18646)
- Symptom reproduced on: macOS 15 + bash 3.2.57 + sudo 1.9.17p2
- User sudoers has `env_keep+="HOME MAIL"` so `$HOME` fallback is safe on this host

title: t2075: fix(interactive-session-helper): `set -e` kills claim flow before `status:in-review` label is applied
body:
## What

`interactive-session-helper.sh claim` silently dies with exit 1 and never applies `status:in-review` or self-assignment, breaking the t2056 interactive issue ownership protocol completely on every call. No output, no warning — the caller has no idea the claim didn't land.

## Why

Lines 265-271 of `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh` carry the same `set -e` exit-propagation bug as GH#18770:

```bash
local had_label=1
_isc_has_in_review "$issue" "$slug"
local has_rc=$?
if [[ $has_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
    had_label=0
fi
```

`_isc_has_in_review` returns 1 as a legitimate "label not present" signal (jq `-e` on an empty match). Under `set -euo pipefail` at the top of the script, an unchecked non-zero return from a called function kills the parent function immediately — before `has_rc=$?` can capture it. The `_isc_cmd_claim` function exits with 1, the caller sees no output, and the issue never gets the `status:in-review` label.

**Reproduced on:** bash 3.2.57 (macOS), bash 4+ (Linux) — `set -e` behaviour is identical on both. Traced with `bash -x`:

```text
+ local had_label=1
+ _isc_has_in_review 18784 marcusquinn/aidevops
+ jq -e ...
+ return 1
(script dies here, `local has_rc=$?` never runs)
```

Impact: every interactive session that tries to claim an issue goes through this path. The pulse dispatch-dedup guard relies on `status:in-review` being set to block worker dispatch on an issue a human is actively working on (t2056). With this bug, that protection is silently disabled — the race between interactive claim and pulse dispatch is wide open.

This is the **same bug pattern** as GH#18770 (set -e + `local var=$(f)` capture) and GH#18784 (set -e + unguarded getent) — a systemic class. The new `bash-compat.md` pre-merge checklist item (from PR #18785) specifically calls this out as checklist item 4.

## How

Replace lines 265-271 with a `set -e`-safe idiom. Two equivalent fixes:

**Option A** (explicit rc capture):

```bash
local had_label=1
local has_rc=0
_isc_has_in_review "$issue" "$slug" || has_rc=$?
if [[ $has_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
    had_label=0
fi
```

**Option B** (direct conditional — cleaner):

```bash
local had_label=1
if _isc_has_in_review "$issue" "$slug"; then
    had_label=0
fi
```

Option B is preferred — it is shorter, idiomatic, and avoids the rc variable entirely. The function is already being called for its return code; there is no reason to split the call from the branch.

Also audit line 355 (`_isc_has_in_review "$issue" "$slug"` in `_isc_cmd_release`) for the same pattern. If it's a bare call followed by `$?` capture, apply the same fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `interactive-session-helper.sh claim <N> <slug>` successfully applies `status:in-review` when the label is absent
- [ ] `interactive-session-helper.sh claim <N> <slug>` is idempotent when the label is already present (refreshes stamp, exits 0)
- [ ] No bare function calls followed by `$?` capture remain in `interactive-session-helper.sh`
- [ ] Regression test added covering the "label absent" path end-to-end with a stub `gh` and `set -e` enabled
- [ ] `bash -x interactive-session-helper.sh claim 18784 marcusquinn/aidevops` shows the full code path executing (not dying at `_isc_has_in_review`)

## Context

- Originating commit: 72f4bb1f2 (t2056, PR #18744) — the helper was brand new and the pattern was not reviewed for `set -e` propagation
- Sibling instance of the same bug class: GH#18770 (pulse-wrapper.sh self-check), GH#18784 (aidevops.sh getent)
- Pre-merge checklist that should have caught this: `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md` (from PR #18785) → "Cross-platform command portability" → item 4
- Affected protocol: t2056 "Interactive issue ownership" in `.agents/AGENTS.md` and `prompts/build.txt`

title: t2076: feat(tooling): add static scanner for unguarded Linux/macOS-only command calls in shell scripts
body:
## What

Add a static scanner that greps all `.sh` files in the repo for unguarded calls to Linux-only commands (getent, readlink -f, stat --format, date -d, sed -r, grep -P, timeout, sha256sum, base64 -w, find -printf, xargs -r, mktemp --suffix) and macOS-only commands (dscl, sw_vers, launchctl, pbcopy, defaults, security, codesign), and fails CI if any unguarded usage is found.

## Why

PR #18785 (t2074, GH#18784) added a comprehensive table of cross-platform command divergences to `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md`, but the rules are documentation-only — there is no automated enforcement. Three production bugs in the same week were all caused by unguarded command calls that would have been caught by a grep-based scanner:

- **GH#18784** — `getent passwd` unguarded in `aidevops.sh`, broke macOS
- **GH#18770** — `_pulse_handle_self_check` set-e propagation (adjacent bug class, same pre-merge checklist)
- **t1983 (GH#18423)** — BSD awk dynamic-regex construct silently broke on macOS

The guarded pattern is easy to detect:
- Unguarded: `getent passwd ...`
- Guarded: `command -v getent &>/dev/null && getent passwd ...` OR preceded by `[[ "$(uname)" == "Linux" ]]`

## How

Create `.agents/scripts/lint-shell-portability.sh` that:

1. Enumerates all tracked `.sh` files via `git ls-files "*.sh"` (excluding `tests/` optionally).
2. For each file, scans for each Linux-only/macOS-only command pattern from the table in `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md`.
3. For each hit, verifies the same physical line or the 3-5 preceding lines contain one of:
   - `command -v <cmd>` guard
   - `[[ "$(uname)" == "Darwin" ]]` or `[[ "$(uname)" == "Linux" ]]` branch
   - An already-portable wrapper name (from the "canonical portable wrappers" table in bash-compat.md)
4. Emits one error per unguarded hit with `file:line: unguarded <cmd>` format.
5. Returns non-zero if any errors.

Then add a CI job `.github/workflows/shell-portability.yml` that runs the scanner on PR changes (or full scan on main push) and blocks merge on failure.

### Scanner design notes

- **Use rg, not grep** — `rg` has faster startup and better file-type filtering.
- **Patterns should be regex-anchored** — `\bgetent\s+passwd\b` not just `getent`, to avoid matching comments/strings.
- **Allow an inline suppression** — comment marker `# shell-portability: ignore next` for the rare legitimate case.
- **Don't scan `bash-compat.md` or the scanner itself** — they contain the patterns as documentation.
- **Test the scanner** with a fixture file that deliberately contains both guarded and unguarded usages, assert the scanner flags the unguarded ones and passes the guarded ones.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.agents/scripts/lint-shell-portability.sh` exists and is executable
- [ ] Scanner finds the exact bug pattern from GH#18784 when run against the pre-fix `aidevops.sh` (regression-style test)
- [ ] Scanner passes cleanly on current main
- [ ] Fixture-based unit test in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-lint-shell-portability.sh` covering 5+ guarded and 5+ unguarded examples
- [ ] `.github/workflows/shell-portability.yml` runs the scanner on PRs
- [ ] `linters-local.sh` includes the scanner in its local-run list so developers catch issues before push

## Context

- Precedent: `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md` (PR #18785) — the full pattern table
- Adjacent work: `prompts/build.txt` → "ShellCheck zero violations" already exists as a separate rule; this extends the quality bar to coreutils portability
- Related bug class: set -e + function return code capture (3 prod hits in one week: GH#18770, GH#18784, GH#18786). A second lint rule could catch `$(f); local rc=$?` without a preceding `|| has_rc=$?` — tracked separately if this PR grows too large.

title: t2077: research: add macOS runner to CI matrix for shell-script regression tests
body:
## What

Decide whether to add a macOS runner to the GitHub Actions matrix for shell-script jobs, and implement if the answer is yes. Today only Ubuntu runs, which means macOS-specific regressions (BSD coreutils vs GNU, bash 3.2 vs 4+, dscl vs getent) slip through CI unchallenged.

## Why

Three P0 production bugs in the same week were caused by Linux/macOS shell divergences that would have been caught by a macOS CI run:

- **GH#18784 (t2074)** — `aidevops.sh` getent unguarded. Caught locally when the user ran `sudo aidevops approve` on macOS; CI was green.
- **GH#18770** — `pulse-wrapper.sh` _pulse_handle_self_check set-e propagation. The pulse has been dead on the user's macOS since 3.8.13 auto-deployed ~27 hours before detection.
- **t1983 (GH#18423)** — BSD awk dynamic-regex construct broke `add_gh_ref_to_todo` on macOS for weeks before surfacing.

Each of these shipped to green CI, and each was caught only when the user ran the broken code on their Mac. The framework's *primary* user is on macOS. The framework's *CI matrix* has zero macOS coverage.

This is an asymmetric cost-of-failure problem: Ubuntu-only CI is cheap but catches nothing macOS-specific; macOS runners cost ~10x ($0.08/min vs $0.008/min on GitHub-hosted) but would catch exactly the class of bugs we keep shipping.

The `.github/workflows/bash-compat-check.yml` workflow already exists but (per the workflow name) it is a *pattern scanner*, not an actual bash 3.2 execution test. It cannot catch runtime divergences like "getent doesn't exist on BSD" — only an actual macOS runner can.

## Decision questions

1. **Full matrix or targeted jobs?** Running the entire CI matrix on macOS doubles run-time and cost. A targeted approach: run ShellCheck on both OSes (already the case — `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` is green), plus the new portability-scanner (GH#18787 if implemented), plus specific regression tests like `test-aidevops-sh-portability.sh` on macOS only.
2. **Which jobs MUST run on macOS?**
   - ShellCheck (already running on both — good)
   - `test-aidevops-sh-portability.sh` — only meaningful on macOS (structural test passes anywhere, but the runtime simulation benefits from real BSD coreutils)
   - `test-pulse-*` suite — the pulse is the hottest source of bugs; running its unit tests on macOS is the highest-ROI addition
   - `test-interactive-session-helper.sh` (GH#18786 fix) — same rationale
3. **Frequency?** Every PR vs only on main vs nightly. PR-level is safest but costliest; main-only + nightly is a reasonable compromise.
4. **Cost envelope?** GitHub-hosted `macos-latest` is ~$0.08/minute. Estimate 5 min/run × 10 runs/day × 30 days = 1500 min/month ≈ $120/month. Acceptable if it catches one production bug per week.
5. **Self-hosted alternative?** The user already runs the pulse on their Mac mini. Could add a self-hosted macOS runner for free, but adds operational overhead and security considerations for an OSS repo accepting external PRs.

## Recommendation (to be debated in this issue)

Add `macos-latest` to the existing `ShellCheck` matrix (already done), plus:

1. New job `test-suite-macos` running the highest-value test scripts on macOS-latest only on main branch pushes (not every PR). Targets: `test-aidevops-sh-portability.sh`, `test-pulse-wrapper-self-check.sh` (once the GH#18770 canary lands), `test-interactive-session-helper.sh` (once GH#18786 lands).
2. Nightly scheduled run of the full test suite on macOS-latest — catches drift without blocking individual PRs.
3. Do NOT run SonarCloud, CodeFactor, Codacy, Socket, etc. on macOS — those tools are OS-agnostic and running them twice is pure cost.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decision documented in this issue with cost estimate and scope
- [ ] If approved: new `.github/workflows/test-suite-macos.yml` or equivalent addition to existing workflow
- [ ] Scoped to main-branch pushes + nightly schedule (not every PR, to keep cost proportional)
- [ ] Documents the canary tests running on macOS in `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md` pre-merge checklist item 2

## Out of scope

- Full matrix expansion (Windows, Linux variants) — macOS is the critical gap
- Self-hosted runners — operational overhead + external-PR security is a separate conversation

## Context

- Related: GH#18784 (getent bug), GH#18770 (pulse-wrapper set -e), GH#18423 (BSD awk)
- Reference: `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md` → "Pre-merge checklist for scripts that touch external commands" (added in PR #18785)
- Note: this is explicitly a tier:reasoning decision task, not a tier:simple implementation task, because the trade-off between cost and safety is a judgment call the maintainer needs to make.

title: t2079: fix: investigate/fix `StandardOutput=` quoting in `_systemd_escape` across 3 service generators
body:
## What

Three service-file generators in the codebase emit `StandardOutput=` and `StandardError=` directives with values that have been passed through `_systemd_escape()`, which wraps the value in literal double-quotes. Investigate whether systemd strips those outer quotes at parse time for StandardOutput= (like it does for Environment= and ExecStart=) or whether they become part of the literal filename. Fix all three sites if the bug is confirmed.

## Why

Scope-split finding from the review of GH#18770. The `_systemd_escape` helper wraps its output in `"..."` (setup-modules/schedulers.sh:554: `printf `%s`). It is used in three places:

- `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:663-664` — generic scheduler install
- `.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh:1566-1567` — auto-update systemd unit
- `.agents/scripts/repo-sync-helper.sh:657` — repo-sync systemd unit

If systemd does NOT strip outer quotes from StandardOutput= values, **all three** generators produce broken units: systemd tries to create a file literally named `"append:/path/to/log"` (with the quote characters) which fails, and the service output is silently discarded.

## Investigation plan

### Step 1: Read the systemd docs

- `man systemd.exec` → `StandardOutput=` section: does it follow shell-like or literal-string quoting?
- `man systemd.syntax` → generic unit-file quoting rules
- https://systemd.io/ESCAPE_CODES — systemd value escaping spec

### Step 2: Reproduce on a real systemd system

```bash
cat > /tmp/test.service <<EOF
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/bin/true
StandardOutput="append:/tmp/systemd-quote-test.log"
EOF
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user --wait start $(realpath /tmp/test.service)
ls -la "/tmp/systemd-quote-test.log" 2>&1
```

Whichever filename was created (or not) answers the question definitively.

### Step 3a: If the bug is confirmed

Remove the `_systemd_escape` wrapping from these specific call sites. Prefer inline bare values — the log path is a plain filesystem path with no shell metacharacters.

```diff
-${_service_extra}${_env_lines}StandardOutput=$(_systemd_escape "append:${log_file}")
-StandardError=$(_systemd_escape "append:${log_file}")
+${_service_extra}${_env_lines}StandardOutput=append:${log_file}
+StandardError=append:${log_file}
```

### Step 3b: If the bug is NOT confirmed

Add inline comments at each site citing the systemd man-page section that confirms quotes are stripped, so future reviewers do not redo this investigation.

### Step 4: Regardless — add a canary test

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-systemd-unit-generation.sh` that generates a unit file, runs `systemd-analyze verify` against it, and asserts it passes. This catches future regressions on Linux CI runners at PR time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Authoritative answer documented: does systemd strip outer quotes from StandardOutput= value?
- [ ] If bug confirmed: all three sites fixed

title: t2080: test: add canary for `pulse-wrapper.sh main()` runtime execution
body:
## What

Add a tier:simple canary test that sources `pulse-wrapper.sh` and invokes `main --self-check` (or equivalent no-op entry point), asserting the script reaches the canary line without crashing. This would have caught PR #18712's `_pulse_handle_self_check` `set -e` regression (GH#18770) at CI time instead of letting it auto-deploy and kill the pulse on the user's machine for 27 hours.

## Why

GH#18770 root-caused a regression where `_pulse_handle_self_check` function returned non-zero under normal operation, and the caller captured it via an unchecked pattern that let `set -e` kill the script before it could continue. The bug was completely invisible to:

- ShellCheck (neither macOS nor Linux caught it — the pattern is syntactically valid)
- SonarCloud, Codacy, CodeFactor (no dynamic analysis, just static code smell detection)
- CodeRabbit (review said "looks good")
- The existing test suite (which only grep-tests the generated unit-file *text*, not runtime execution)

The only way to catch this class of bug is to **actually run pulse-wrapper.sh** under `bash -e` and see if it reaches a known checkpoint. The test doesn't need to do anything useful — just source the script, call a dispatcher with a mode that early-exits cleanly, and assert exit 0.

This is the same pattern already in use for `aidevops.sh` (`bash aidevops.sh --version` is run in the version-consistency CI job — ships with a predictable exit 0 that confirms the script parses and executes through its initialisation block). The pulse wrapper has no equivalent.

## How

### Option A — real main() invocation with short-circuit

Add a `--canary` flag to `pulse-wrapper.sh` `main()` that:

1. Sources the script (all top-level declarations run under `set -euo pipefail`)
2. Runs `_pulse_handle_self_check` (the exact function GH#18770 broke)
3. Runs `acquire_instance_lock` (the next function downstream)
4. Immediately releases the lock and exits 0
5. Does NOT actually enter the pulse loop, dispatch workers, or make any GitHub API calls

Then a test at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh` just runs:

```bash
FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS=1 timeout 30 bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh --canary
rc=$?
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || { echo "FAIL: pulse-wrapper --canary exited $rc"; exit 1; }
```

### Option B — extracted function test (lower-effort)

Source `pulse-wrapper.sh` in a harness, call `_pulse_handle_self_check` directly with stubbed inputs, assert the return code is 0. Catches the specific bug but not downstream regressions.

Prefer **Option A** — it catches more classes of regression at the cost of a slightly more invasive change to pulse-wrapper.sh.

### Option C — add to existing linters-local.sh quality-check loop

Once Option A lands, add the canary to `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` so developers catch the regression before push (not just at CI time).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pulse-wrapper.sh --canary` (or equivalent no-op entry mode) exists and exits 0 when the script parses and initialises cleanly
- [ ] `test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh` exists, runs the canary with a 30s timeout, asserts exit 0
- [ ] Canary test is wired into CI (add to the existing test-suite job, not a new workflow)
- [ ] Canary test is added to `linters-local.sh` for pre-push execution
- [ ] Regression verification: run the test against the pre-fix `pulse-wrapper.sh` HEAD (before GH#18770's fix) and confirm it fails with the same exit 2 the user saw

## Context

- Originating: GH#18770 review comment by me, scope-split from the main fix PR
- Sibling test: `tests/test-pulse-systemd-timeout.sh` (grep-based only, did not catch GH#18770)
- Reference: the same "test the script under set -e" principle is already applied to `aidevops.sh` via the version-consistency CI job
- Related: `bash-compat.md` pre-merge checklist item 4 (added in PR #18785) — this canary is the enforcement for that checklist item on the pulse

title: t2081: fix: CodeRabbit auto-review silently skipped on all internal PRs due to single-exclusion label config
body:
## What

CodeRabbit is silently skipping auto-review on all internal PRs with this message:

> Auto reviews are limited based on label configuration.
> Review skipped — only excluded labels are configured. (1) no-review

The `.coderabbit.yaml` config has a single label entry `- "!no-review"` (an exclusion filter), which CodeRabbit interprets as "empty inclusion list, skip all PRs" instead of "review everything except PRs labeled no-review".

## Why

Repeat bug — GH#17904 already removed a positive `external-contributor` label that was inadvertently disabling internal PR reviews. The config comment at `.coderabbit.yaml:47-54` documents the lesson: "Do NOT add positive labels here; use path_filters or path_instructions". But the config left only the single exclusion entry, which CodeRabbit now treats as the same failure mode.

Observable impact on PR #18785 (just merged):

```
> Review skipped — only excluded labels are configured. (1) no-review
```

The review-bot-gate passed only because CodeRabbit emits a commit status independent of formal reviews (`commit_status: true` in config, line 68), which the helper uses as a fallback signal. But the actual code review — the reason we pay for CodeRabbit Pro — is not happening.

## Investigation needed

1. Confirm the exact CodeRabbit schema semantics for `reviews.auto_review.labels` with only exclusion entries:
   - Does `["!no-review"]` mean "review PRs unless they have no-review" (intuitive)?
   - Or does it mean "only review PRs in the inclusion set (empty) and also exclude no-review" (observed)?
   - CodeRabbit docs: https://docs.coderabbit.ai/guides/review-instructions
2. Test fix candidates on a scratch branch (so the main repo isn't at risk):
   - **Candidate A**: remove the `labels` list entirely; rely on default behaviour.
   - **Candidate B**: add a wildcard positive entry like `- "*"` if the schema supports it.
   - **Candidate C**: add the full list of expected internal-PR labels positively (e.g. `origin:interactive`, `origin:worker`, `tier:simple`, `tier:standard`, `tier:reasoning`, `bug`, `enhancement`).
3. Once a candidate is proven, apply to `.coderabbit.yaml` with a comment citing this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CodeRabbit config semantics confirmed via docs or testing
- [ ] `.coderabbit.yaml` updated so auto-review runs on internal PRs by default
- [ ] Test on a real PR: open a trivial change, verify CodeRabbit posts an actual review (not a skip message)
- [ ] Comment in `.coderabbit.yaml` warns the next reviewer not to repeat the single-exclusion mistake

## Context

- Prior incident: GH#17904 removed `external-contributor` positive label after the same symptom
- Current config: `.coderabbit.yaml:55-56` — `labels: [- "!no-review"]`
- Prior context comment: `.coderabbit.yaml:47-54`
- Observed on: PR #18785 (t2074, getent fix) — Review ID `bbfa3c34-662f-462a-b389-fe6896aceedd`
- Impact: low severity (review-bot-gate has commit-status fallback, so merge path still works), but we're paying for CodeRabbit Pro and getting zero review value

## Severity

Low-priority from a correctness standpoint (the fallback keeps merges safe), but high-priority from a cost/value standpoint — we're paying for a service that is silently no-op on the majority of PRs.

title: t2083: fix(pulse-dispatch): Deterministic fill floor silently rejects all candidates without logging skip reasons
body:
## What

The `Deterministic fill floor` pass emits a `candidates=N` count followed by `Adaptive settle wait: 0 dispatches` with no per-candidate logging when every candidate is silently rejected. Observed on 2026-04-14 post-GH#18770 fix (first clean cycle of v3.8.17):

```
[pulse-wrapper] Early fill floor: dispatching workers before housekeeping
[pulse-wrapper] Deterministic fill floor: available=24, runnable=22, queued_without_worker=0, candidates=22
[0;32m[SUCCESS][0m Resolved opus -> anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (primary)
[pulse-wrapper] dispatch_triage_reviews: parsed 11 candidates from state file
... (11 triage skip lines) ...
[pulse-wrapper] dispatch_triage_reviews: dispatched 0 triage workers (24 slots remaining)
[0;32m[SUCCESS][0m Resolved opus -> anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (primary)
[pulse-wrapper] Adaptive settle wait (fill floor): 0 dispatches — skipping wait
[pulse-wrapper] Stage start: complexity_scan (timeout 600s)
```

22 candidates → 0 dispatched. No `Deterministic fill floor complete:` line. No `Launch validation failed`. No `BLOCKED`. No `skipping`. No `Dispatched worker PID`. Just silence.

## Why

The likely culprit is `_dff_should_skip_candidate` at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:266`, specifically the `check_terminal_blockers` call which is invoked with `>/dev/null 2>&1` suppressing all output:

```bash
_dff_should_skip_candidate() {
    if check_terminal_blockers "$issue_number" "$repo_slug" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        return 0   # skip silently
    fi
    ...
}
```

If `check_terminal_blockers` is matching every candidate (e.g., because of stale state from a crash, a bad regex match on a common substring, or a label check that false-positives), every candidate is silently rejected with no log entry explaining why. The only symptom is `candidates=N, dispatched=0` with nothing between.

Alternative root causes to investigate:
1. `check_terminal_blockers` false-positive on all 22 candidates
2. `dispatch_with_dedup` returning non-zero silently on all candidates
3. `_dff_process_candidate` hitting a `set -e` kill at a point before the function returns
4. `candidates_json` being truncated somehow between the `candidates=22` log and the while-read loop

Note: this is the same class of symptom the framework has now hit three times in one week (GH#18770, GH#18784, GH#18786) — a silent failure where a `set -e` or unchecked return swallows the error. Adding mandatory debug logging at each skip site would make this class of bug self-diagnosing.

## How

### Step 1: Add mandatory per-candidate skip logging

Every `_dff_should_skip_candidate` early-return path MUST log which check fired. Currently only `fast_fail_is_skipped`, the placeholder-body check, and the stub-body check log. `check_terminal_blockers` does NOT log from the caller — and the caller intentionally redirects its stdout/stderr to /dev/null.

Proposed: either (a) log `[pulse-wrapper] Deterministic fill floor: skipping #{issue} ({repo}) — terminal blocker detected` unconditionally when `check_terminal_blockers` returns true, OR (b) remove the `>/dev/null 2>&1` redirect so check_terminal_blockers`s own log lines are visible.

Option (b) is cleaner — trust the helper to log its own reason.

### Step 2: Add a `PULSE_DEBUG` flag that bypasses the skip checks

When `PULSE_DEBUG=1` is set, `_dff_process_candidate` should log the candidate's labels, dedup state, and skip outcome before making the skip decision. This gives operators a way to debug silent-dispatch failures without modifying code.

### Step 3: Add a regression test

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-silent-dispatch.sh` — constructs a mock `_dff_should_skip_candidate` that rejects all candidates, runs the dispatch loop, asserts that EACH rejection is logged. Catches future silent-failure regressions at CI time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every `_dff_should_skip_candidate` early-return path writes a log line naming the check that fired
- [ ] The `check_terminal_blockers` call no longer uses `>/dev/null 2>&1` (its own log output reaches the pulse log)
- [ ] `PULSE_DEBUG=1` adds per-candidate debug output (labels, dedup-probe results, skip decision)
- [ ] Test `test-pulse-wrapper-silent-dispatch.sh` exists and asserts every skip is logged
- [ ] Running the current cycle with `PULSE_DEBUG=1` reveals WHY the 22 candidates in the Early fill floor pass were all silently rejected

## Context

- Observed: 2026-04-14 03:22 UTC, first clean pulse cycle after v3.8.17 (GH#18770 fix) deployed
- Log file: `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` byte offset 19879048
- Source files: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:266-295` (`_dff_should_skip_candidate`), `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:2263` (`check_terminal_blockers`)
- Same bug class as GH#18770, GH#18784, GH#18786 — silent return-code propagation failures
- Related: pre-merge checklist item 4 in `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md` (from PR #18785) warns about exactly this class

title: bug: _close_conflicting_pr auto-closes implementation PRs when a planning PR with the same task ID has merged
body:
## Bug: `_close_conflicting_pr` false-positive auto-close — confused planning PRs with implementation PRs

**Severity:** high — direct cause of lost work in production.

**Real-world incident (2026-04-14):** PR #18760 (`t2060: fix(task-complete-helper): move completed entries to ## Done`) was auto-closed by `pulse-merge.sh:_close_conflicting_pr` with the false claim:

> Closing — this PR has merge conflicts with the base branch. The work for this task (`t2060`) has already landed on main (via PR #18749), so no re-attempt is needed.

In reality:

- PR #18749 was titled `plan(t2059, t2060): file follow-ups from GH#18538 worker-is-triager session` — a planning-only PR that added `todo/tasks/t2059-brief.md` + `todo/tasks/t2060-brief.md` and one TODO.md edit. **No implementation files were touched.**
- PR #18760 actually implemented the fix in `task-complete-helper.sh` + `tests/test-task-complete-move.sh` + a 561-entry TODO.md cleanup. **None of that ever landed on main.**
- Issue #18746 is still **OPEN**.

The deterministic merge pass extracted the task ID `t2060` from PR #18760's title, fetched recent main commit subjects, ran `grep -iE "(^|[^a-zA-Z0-9])t2060([^a-zA-Z0-9]|$)"`, and matched the substring `, t2060)` in the planning PR's commit subject. The grep cannot distinguish a planning commit from an implementation commit.

## Blast radius

- `gh search prs --state closed --merged=false "has already landed on main"` returns exactly 2 PRs in the repo's entire history. One (#18584 / t2045) was a legitimate dedup. The other (#18760) was this false positive. **50% false-positive rate** on the only two cases that have ever existed.
- The bug will recur every time a planning-brief PR for a task is merged before the implementation PR for the same task — which is the **standard flow** under `claim-task-id.sh` + `/define`.

## Root cause

`pulse-merge.sh:_close_conflicting_pr` (lines 1097-1136):

```bash
matching_subject=$(printf '%s\n' "$commit_subjects" |
    grep -iE "(^|[^a-zA-Z0-9])${task_id_from_pr}([^a-zA-Z0-9]|$)" |
    head -1)

if [[ -n "$matching_subject" ]]; then
    work_on_main="true"
    # → closes PR with "already landed" message
fi
```

The function already knows that auto-closing the linked **issue** is unsafe (GH#17642 explicitly leaves issues open). But it auto-closes **PRs** based on the same heuristic — and a closed PR with no auto-issue-close means the issue stays open while the work that would close it gets discarded.

## Fix

**File-overlap verification before closing.** A real implementation duplicate must touch at least one non-planning file in common with the closing PR.

1. Change the commits fetch to return `(sha, subject)` pairs instead of subjects only.
2. When a subject match is found, fetch the matching commit's files (`gh api repos/.../commits/SHA`) AND the closing PR's files (`gh pr view ... --json files`).
3. Compute the intersection, excluding planning paths: `TODO.md`, `README.md`, `todo/**`, `.agents/configs/simplification-state.json`, `*.md` files inside `todo/tasks/`.
4. If the intersection is **empty** → false positive. Do **NOT** close. Post an idempotent `_post_rebase_nudge_on_worker_conflicting` comment (modelled on `_post_rebase_nudge_on_interactive_conflicting`) and return.
5. If file lookups fail (network error) → fail-CLOSED: do NOT auto-close, post nudge, log warning. Better to leave a stuck PR than to lose work.
6. If the intersection has at least one implementation file → genuine duplicate → close as today.

## Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — refactor `_close_conflicting_pr` (lines 1074-1168), add `_post_rebase_nudge_on_worker_conflicting` helper modelled on `_post_rebase_nudge_on_interactive_conflicting` at line 1012.
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-close-conflicting-pr-wording.sh` — update the existing 3 tests to match the new TSV stub contract; add 2 new regression tests:
  - `test_no_close_when_matching_commit_only_touches_planning_files` — reproduces the #18760 false positive
  - `test_close_when_matching_commit_overlaps_implementation_files` — confirms genuine duplicates still close

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-close-conflicting-pr-wording.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-close-conflicting-pr-wording.sh  # 5/5 pass
```

Then post-merge: confirm the patch release ships and the bug cannot recur on a fresh run.

## Recovery for already-affected work

PR #18760 has been reopened (see comment trail). The branch `feature/auto-20260414-012652` is still on origin so the implementation, test harness, and 561-entry TODO.md cleanup are recoverable in full once this fix is in.

## Why urgent

Lost work in a rapid-pipeline framework is unacceptable. Every dispatch cycle that runs the buggy merge pass risks closing real implementation PRs as soon as their planning brief PR has merged. Patch release.

title: design call: classify _is_stale_assignment() gh-API failure path — fail-OPEN (current) vs fail-CLOSED
body:
## Follow-up: classification disagreement on `_is_stale_assignment()` gh-API failure path

The t2046 Deliverable A audit completed in PR #18765 classified `_is_stale_assignment()`'s gh-API failure path (`dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:455-457`) as **appropriately fail-OPEN** under deadlock-recovery semantics:

```bash
comments_json=$(gh api "repos/${repo_slug}/issues/${issue_number}/comments" \
    --jq '...' 2>/dev/null) || comments_json="[]"
```

A duplicate parallel session (PR #18805, since closed as duplicate) independently reached the **opposite** conclusion: that this is fail-OPEN in the wrong direction, because:

> A gh-API failure → `comments_json="[]"` → no dispatch claim comment found → recover stale assignment → return 0 → unblock dispatch. This can undo `is_assigned()`'s protection on a transient gh-API hiccup, dispatching a duplicate worker against an issue that has a real active claim.

PR #18805's closing comment flagged this for follow-up but the issue was never filed — this issue exists to track the design call.

## What needs deciding

1. **Is the deadlock-recovery argument correct?** `_is_stale_assignment` exists to recover from worker crashes mid-dispatch. If gh API is down, dispatching another worker against a possibly-active issue is arguably better than letting the issue stall forever.
2. **Or is the duplicate-dispatch argument correct?** A transient gh API blip is more common than a worker crash. Failing CLOSED on API errors keeps existing claims intact and only delays dispatch by one pulse cycle (until gh recovers).
3. **Or both?** Differentiate API-error fail-modes by attempt count or timeout: first failure → fail-CLOSED (return 1, keep block), N failures over M minutes → fail-OPEN (recover stale).

## Context

- `_is_stale_assignment` is the only guard between `is_assigned()` and dispatch. If it incorrectly returns 0 (stale → safe to dispatch), the entire dedup chain is bypassed.
- The current threshold is 10 minutes (`STALE_ASSIGNMENT_THRESHOLD_SECONDS=600`), so a transient gh outage would need to span an entire pulse cycle to actually fire this path on every check.
- Test coverage: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-fail-closed.sh` covers the rest of the audit but not this specific path.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:445-499` (`_is_stale_assignment` definition)
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:455-457` (the contested line)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-fail-closed.sh` (where any new test would live)

## Decision

Up to whoever owns the dispatch-dedup design. This issue exists so the question doesn't get lost in PR #18805's closed comment thread.

## Lineage

- t2046 (Deliverable A audit, parent) — GH#18458 / parent-task
- t2061 — original audit task — closed via PR #18765 (merged)
- PR #18805 — duplicate session, closed by author with this question raised

title: feat(scan-stale): detect closed-not-merged PRs whose linked issue is still open
body:
## Enhancement: extend `interactive-session-helper.sh scan-stale` to detect closed-PR-with-open-issue mismatches

## Problem

Today's stale-claim scan (`interactive-session-helper.sh scan-stale`) checks for issues claimed by a now-dead session (PID gone, worktree missing). It does not detect a more pernicious failure mode: **a closed-not-merged PR whose linked issue is still open and unassigned.**

This was the failure mode that hid PR #18760's loss until the user happened to glance at their GitHub inbox. The pulse closed the PR, the issue stayed open with `status:queued`, the worker that would have noticed was already done, and the cleanup loop saw nothing wrong because no session was holding the issue.

## What `scan-stale` should add

For every repo in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` with `pulse: true`:

1. List PRs that are: state=CLOSED, mergedAt=null, closedAt within the last 14 days.
2. For each, fetch `closingIssuesReferences` and the linked issue numbers from the body (`Resolves #N`, `Closes #N`, `Fixes #N`, `For #N`).
3. For each linked issue, check if it's still OPEN.
4. If yes, surface it as a **stale recovery candidate**:

   ```
   STALE: PR #18760 (closed not merged) → issue #18746 still OPEN
     Title: t2060: fix(task-complete-helper) ...
     Branch: feature/auto-20260414-012652 (still on origin: yes/no)
     Closed by: deterministic merge pass (pulse-merge.sh) / author / other
     Action: gh pr reopen 18760 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops
   ```

5. Don't auto-reopen — surface it for the human to triage. Auto-reopening a PR that was legitimately closed (e.g. genuinely superseded by a different fix) would be just as bad as the original close.

## Optional Phase 2

If the closing comment was posted by `pulse-merge.sh` (matching the `_Closed by deterministic merge pass_` marker), elevate the report to a higher severity tier — those are exactly the cases where the heuristic may have lied.

## Why this matters

The aidevops state machine is GitHub issues + PRs. The user's attention mechanism is the gh inbox. A closed PR linked to a still-open issue is invisible in both: PR is closed (not in the open-PRs list), issue is unassigned (not in the assignee's view). The only place it surfaces is when a human notices the orphaned issue in passing — which is exactly the failure that motivated this issue.

The scan-stale extension closes that visibility gap in the framework's own audit interface.

## Files

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh` — extend `scan_stale` (or add `scan_orphaned_issues`) to enumerate closed-not-merged PRs cross-repo and check their linked-issue state.
- **EDIT:** `~/.aidevops/agents/AGENTS.md` "Interactive issue ownership" section — document the new behaviour.

## Verification

- Stub a closed-not-merged PR with a linked OPEN issue, run `scan-stale`, assert it surfaces the mismatch.
- Stub a closed-not-merged PR with a linked CLOSED issue, run `scan-stale`, assert it does NOT surface (legitimate close).

## Severity

Medium. This is a defensive backstop — the upstream fix (`_close_conflicting_pr` overlap check, separate issue) prevents the false-positive at the source. This catches any other mechanism that closes PRs without closing their issues, including bugs we haven't yet identified.
